info.title: Davix H2I API
info.description: Self-hosted image, PDF, and HTML-rendering processing API. Built on Sharp/libvips, pdf-lib, qpdf, Poppler, and Puppeteer. Every endpoint listed as job_eligible in GET /v1/registry additionally accepts an opt-in `async: true` field (JSON body or multipart field, string "true" or boolean) -- omitted or false, the endpoint behaves exactly as documented below (a synchronous 200); with it set, and an individual customer API key, the endpoint instead responds 202 with {job_id, status_url}, and the same result becomes available via GET /v1/jobs/{id} once finished.

schemes.name: X-Api-Key
schemes.description: Owner, customer, or public-tier API key sent in the X-Api-Key header.
The same API key sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

auth.productionRule: In production an API key in the query string or request body is rejected with 400 api_key_location_not_allowed; only the X-Api-Key header or an Authorization Bearer header are accepted. Official SDKs never send keys any other way.

request.name: Idempotency-Key
request.description: Optional. Reusing the same key for a materially different request (different file/parameter set) is rejected with 409 idempotency_key_conflict; reusing it for an identical retry safely avoids double-billing. Honoured by quota-metered processing endpoints (see endpoint.idempotency.supported).

request.name: X-Davix-App
request.description: Optional. The name of the app that makes this call, for example "My shop importer": the same as the `app` field. Shown in your History next to the result. Up to 60 characters.

response.name: Request-Id
response.description: Unique id of this request (also returned as `request_id` in JSON bodies). Quote it to support.

response.name: Retry-After
response.description: Seconds to wait before retrying; sent with some 429/503 responses.

retry.note: Only statuses the server documents as retryable (error catalog `retryable`). A POST is retried only when the endpoint supports idempotency and a single Idempotency-Key is reused for every attempt of the same logical call.

requestPolicy.note: The SDK refuses absolute URLs, path traversal and anything outside /v1/ so it can never be used to reach internal or admin routes.

AiEnvelope.description: The Davix H2I AI response envelope. `result` holds the feature-specific data (see the linked capability for its shape); provider-specific raw responses are never exposed.

result.description: Feature-specific result. For image features this is {images:[{url,width,height,format,size_bytes}], model_notes}.

total_tokens.description: The provider's own reported total, not a client-side sum.

pricing.description: Per-unit prices as reported by the provider; null when not priced.

AsyncJobAccepted.description: Returned with HTTP 202 when `async: true` was sent. Poll GET /v1/jobs/{id} (status_url).

EndpointAccess.description: Effective per-category access of the plan.

operation.description: The operation of your plan this endpoint belongs to (the plan switches, allows and counts by operation).

allowed.description: false when the plan does not allow this endpoint.

max_input_dimension_px.description: Longest side of an uploaded image (image endpoints, when capped).

count_basis.description: How a multi-file upload counts against the plan.

files.description: Only for endpoints that take files. null values mean no limit.

max_dimension_px.description: Longest side of a result, in pixels.

max_pixels.description: Width x height of a result.

max_dpi.description: Highest PDF render resolution (PDF to images).

output.description: Only for endpoints whose result size you choose. null values mean no limit.

render.description: Only for the HTML render endpoints.

pages.description: Only for the endpoints with a PDF page cap. `max_pages` is the cap that applies to this endpoint; the named ones are the same value under the control's own name.

cost_per_call.description: Customer keys: how many units of the plan's allowance one call (one file on a files plan, one request on a requests plan) uses on this endpoint. 1 unless the plan says otherwise.

monthly_cap.description: Customer keys: the endpoint's own limit per plan period, counted inside the plan's allowance. Absent when the plan sets none.

job_start_rate.description: Customer keys: how many background jobs you may start per window.

items.description: Customer keys: every control your plan has for this endpoint, ready to show as it is. Each item has key, label, group, kind, unit, value (null = no limit), text (the value as a person reads it), chip (a short form, or null), set (true when your plan itself sets it), limited, platform_default and, for a limit that accumulates over a window (request rate, data volume, AI budget, job starts), used. The list follows what the plan editor offers for the endpoint, so a new kind of limit appears here without any change to a client.

formats.description: Only for endpoints that take or produce a format your plan can switch on or off: one boolean per format group (raster_extended, layered_raw, postscript, legacy_office, email, data_extended, markup_text), false = your plan does not include it (the request is refused with 403 format_not_allowed).

allow_url_ingestion.description: false = source_url / url inputs are not allowed.

url_download_max_bytes.description: Largest file fetched from a URL.

ocr_max_pages.description: Most pages one OCR request reads.

ocr_max_languages.description: Most OCR languages in one request.

allow_ocr_extended_languages.description: false = only the standard OCR languages.

allow_async_jobs.description: false = async=true (a background job) is refused on this endpoint with 403 async_not_allowed.

max_active_jobs.description: Most jobs you may have queued or running at once (all endpoints together); more are refused with 429 async_limit_reached.

job_queue_wait_seconds.description: How long a job of yours may wait for a free processing slot before it fails as busy.

records_per_request.description: Most records in one request (the plan control itself; see `records`).

records_per_unit.description: Records that count as one unit (the plan control itself; see `records`).

features.description: Only for endpoints with plan-controlled features. null = no limit.

max_per_request.description: The most records one request may carry (0 = records are not allowed on your plan).

count_basis.description: How records count toward your quota: each record, every N records (records_per_unit), or the whole request as one unit.

records_per_unit.description: 1 = each record counts; N = every N records count as one unit; 0 = the whole request counts as one.

records.description: Only for endpoints that take `records` (one document per record).

capabilities.description: can_read / can_write and, where true, animated, alpha, lossy, vector, multipage.

available.description: Supported and the tool behind it is installed on this server.

allowed.description: The calling key's plan allows it on at least one endpoint that handles it (always true for public/owner keys and core formats).

grid.description: cols, rows and one entry per cell: row, col, x, y, width, height, diffPixels, diffRatio.

hash.description: algorithm, the two hashes, Hamming distance (0-64) and similarity.

ImageComparison.description: The measurements. Which keys appear depends on `metrics`.

file_id.description: The file's id in your file history (customer keys only): pass it to GET /v1/files/{id} to fetch the file again, or DELETE /v1/files/{id} to delete it now.

page.description: For a multi-page source converted page by page: the page this file is (counting from 1).

pages.description: Number of frames in the file when it is animated.

checks.description: One entry per requested check (colors, palette, hash, transparency, quality, efficiency, dimensions, aspectratio, format, animation, ...). The sub-structure depends on the check.

result.description: The synchronous response body of the job (set once completed); each results[] entry carries a `domain` field (image, pdf or render).

expired.description: true once the key stopped working because its own expiry (or the plan window it follows) passed. It stays listed until deleted.

expires_at.description: The expiry the customer chose for this key, if any.

quota_limit.description: The most units this key may use (in the plan's unit), if the customer set one.

usage.description: In GET /v1/keys: used (units this key used of the shared quota in the current period) and unit.

ai_limit.description: The most this key's AI calls may use, in tokens or dollars (ai_limit_unit), if the customer set one. Only on a plan whose AI has an allowance of its own.

ai_limit_unit.description: tokens or usd: what ai_limit counts.

ai_usage.description: In GET /v1/keys, on a plan whose AI counts tokens or dollars: used (what this key's AI calls used in the current period) and unit (tokens or usd).

file_id.description: The file's id in your file history (customer keys only): pass it to GET /v1/files/{id} to fetch the file again, or DELETE /v1/files/{id} to delete it now.

MetadataReport.description: What a change did: counts before and after, what was removed, what was kept on purpose and what identifying is left.

parameters.description: The saved parameter values, keyed by the endpoint's own field names.

kind.description: file = an image, PDF or other file the operation made; text = the text (JSON) an operation answered with, kept like a file.

url.description: Signed download URL; null unless status is "available".

parameters.description: The parameters the request used (secrets and bulky content such as HTML are left out). Null for files recorded before this was kept.

input_names.description: File names of the uploads that were processed.

settings.description: Every setting of the operation that has a value for this file: the ones the request set (source set) and the ones it left alone that have a default (source default). Empty for files recorded before the request details were kept.

app.description: The app that made the file: the name sent in the `app` field or `X-Davix-App` header, or an official client recognised from its User-Agent (for example "Davix H2I plugin"). Null when it is not known.

html.description: The document (HTML templates, not in the list).

css.description: The CSS (HTML templates, not in the list).

warnings.description: Placeholders written like {{...}} that are not valid variable names (they are not replaced).

unit.description: What the quota counts: 'files' (files processed) or 'requests' (requests made), as the plan says.

period_start.description: When the current quota period began (the plan period).

period_end.description: When it ends and the shared quota starts again.

valid.description: true when the real request would be accepted.

errors.description: Every problem found: field, code (invalid_parameter or missing_field), message, and where known value / minimum / maximum / allowed / limit / limit_name.

processed_separately.description: true when several files would each be processed on their own (one result per file).

estimate.description: What the real request would count against the plan.

limits.description: The limits that apply to this endpoint for your key (same as GET /v1/limits).

endpoints.name: Analyze (generic task runner)
endpoints.description:
Run any registered analysis task by id through the universal request. Readiness: unbenchmarked (see GET /v1/ai/capabilities/core.analyze).

Classification: hybrid. Deterministic stages: task registry dispatch.

fields.name: task
fields.description: A task id from GET /v1/ai/capabilities, e.g. "documents.summarize". The rest of the body must match that task's own request shape.

fields.name: presetId
fields.description: Apply a saved preset (create one with POST /v1/presets). Every value stored in the preset is used unless this request sets that field itself. The preset must have been saved for this same endpoint; requires an individual customer API key.

fields.name: app
fields.description: The name of the app that makes this call, for example "My shop importer". It is shown in your History next to the result, so you can tell which app did what. The official apps fill it in themselves (Davix H2I plugin, Davix H2I n8n node, Davix H2I Studio, Davix H2I Customer Portal); when you leave it out, the official SDKs and plugins are recognised from their User-Agent. Up to 60 characters; control characters and angle brackets are removed. The header `X-Davix-App` does the same. It is only a label: it never changes what the call does.

behavior.normalization: plain text, one line, cut to 60 characters; blank = not set

fields.name: source_url
fields.description: Fetch the input from this public http(s) address instead of uploading a file in "files". Send either the file or source_url, not both. Only public addresses on port 80/443 are fetched (never loopback, private, link-local or cloud-metadata addresses), redirects are re-checked, and the download is size- and time-limited; the fetched file is then judged exactly like an upload (content sniffing, format and size limits).

behavior.note: Not an http(s) URL, credentials in the URL, or an address that is not public -> 400 url_blocked; a download that fails, is too slow or redirects too often -> 400 url_fetch_failed; larger than the limit -> 413 file_too_large; a plan without URL input -> 403 format_not_allowed.

fields.name: source_urls
fields.description: A list of public http(s) addresses to fetch as inputs, as a JSON array, for example ["https://example.com/a.pdf","https://example.com/b.pdf"]. They are added to any files you upload: uploaded files come first, then the URLs, in the order sent. Together they cannot exceed the files-per-request limit of your plan. Only public addresses on port 80/443 are fetched (never loopback, private, link-local or cloud-metadata addresses), redirects are re-checked, and the download is size- and time-limited; every fetched file is then judged exactly like an upload (content sniffing, format and size limits).

behavior.note: Not an http(s) URL, credentials in the URL, or an address that is not public -> 400 url_blocked; a download that fails, is too slow or redirects too often -> 400 url_fetch_failed; larger than the limit -> 413 file_too_large; a plan without URL input -> 403 format_not_allowed; a file and a URL for the same input -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: async
fields.description: Opt-in asynchronous execution. With async=true and an individual customer API key the endpoint answers 202 {job_id, status_url} and the result becomes available from GET /v1/jobs/{id}. Omitted/false = the normal synchronous response. All the files of the request belong to one job; the AI answer envelope is the job result (GET /v1/jobs/{id}). Studio never sends it: this is for API calls.

behavior.normalization: only boolean true or the string "true" enables it
behavior.note: With any other key type the request is rejected with 400 async_requires_customer_key.

Classification: ai. Deterministic stages: file type detection from content, native PDF text extraction / OCR for documents, image normalisation (Sharp), deterministic length/format validation of the result.

fields.name: files
fields.description: Image file(s): PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, TIFF, AVIF, SVG, BMP, ICO, PNM, TGA, DDS, PSD, JPEG XL, JPEG 2000, EPS/AI/PS. Type is detected from content; non-raster formats are converted to PNG before the model sees them. Max 1.

file.note: The operation handles one file per run; send several files in this field and each is processed on its own, answered as one result per file. How many files one request may carry is set by the plan (files per request).

fields.name: model
fields.description: "auto" (dynamically selected) or an explicit OpenRouter model id.

behavior.note: Any other value -> 400 ai_input_invalid.

fields.name: fallback
fields.description: Allow automatic fallback to another eligible model even when `model` is explicit.

fields.name: generation
fields.description: JSON-encoded generation parameters: {temperature,top_p,top_k,max_tokens,seed,frequency_penalty,presence_penalty,stop[]}.

fields.name: instructions
fields.description: Free-form instructions / generation prompt.

fields.name: presetId
fields.description: Apply a saved preset (create one with POST /v1/presets). Every value stored in the preset is used unless this request sets that field itself. The preset must have been saved for this same endpoint; requires an individual customer API key.

fields.name: app
fields.description: The name of the app that makes this call, for example "My shop importer". It is shown in your History next to the result, so you can tell which app did what. Up to 60 characters; control characters and angle brackets are removed. The header `X-Davix-App` does the same. It is only a label: it never changes what the call does.

behavior.normalization: plain text, one line, cut to 60 characters; blank = not set

fields.name: source_url
fields.description: Fetch the input from this public http(s) address instead of uploading a file in "files". Send either the file or source_url, not both. Only public addresses on port 80/443 are fetched (never loopback, private, link-local or cloud-metadata addresses), redirects are re-checked, and the download is size- and time-limited; the fetched file is then judged exactly like an upload (content sniffing, format and size limits).

behavior.note: Not an http(s) URL, credentials in the URL, or an address that is not public -> 400 url_blocked; a download that fails, is too slow or redirects too often -> 400 url_fetch_failed; larger than the limit -> 413 file_too_large; a plan without URL input -> 403 format_not_allowed.

fields.name: async
fields.description: Opt-in asynchronous execution. Omitted/false = the normal synchronous response. All the files of the request belong to one job; the AI answer envelope is the job result (GET /v1/jobs/{id}). behavior.normalization: only boolean true or the string "true" enables it
behavior.note: With any other key type the request is rejected with 400 async_requires_customer_key.

response.description: The Davix H2I AI response envelope.

Only public addresses on port 80/443 are fetched (never loopback, private, link-local or cloud-metadata addresses), redirects are re-checked, and the download is size- and time-limited; the fetched file is then judged exactly like an upload (content sniffing, format and size limits).

behavior.note: Not an http(s) URL, credentials in the URL, or an address that is not public -> 400 url_blocked; a download that fails, is too slow or redirects too often -> 400 url_fetch_failed; larger than the limit -> 413 file_too_large; a plan without URL input -> 403 format_not_allowed.

fields.name: source_urls
fields.description: A list of public http(s) addresses to fetch as inputs, as a JSON array, for example ["https://example.com/a.pdf","https://example.com/b.pdf"]. They are added to any files you upload: uploaded files come first, then the URLs, in the order sent. Together they cannot exceed the files-per-request limit of your plan. Only public addresses on port 80/443 are fetched (never loopback, private, link-local or cloud-metadata addresses), redirects are re-checked, and the download is size- and time-limited; every fetched file is then judged exactly like an upload (content sniffing, format and size limits).

behavior.note: Not an http(s) URL, credentials in the URL, or an address that is not public -> 400 url_blocked; a download that fails, is too slow or redirects too often -> 400 url_fetch_failed; larger than the limit -> 413 file_too_large; a plan without URL input -> 403 format_not_allowed; a file and a URL for the same input -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: async
fields.description: Opt-in asynchronous execution. With async=true and an individual customer API key the endpoint answers 202 {job_id, status_url} and the result becomes available from GET /v1/jobs/{id}. Omitted/false = the normal synchronous response. All the files of the request belong to one job; the AI answer envelope is the job result (GET /v1/jobs/{id}). Studio never sends it: this is for API calls.

behavior.normalization: only boolean true or the string "true" enables it
behavior.note: With any other key type the request is rejected with 400 async_requires_customer_key.

response.description: The Davix H2I AI response envelope.

file.note: The operation handles one file per run; send several files in this field and each is processed on its own, answered as one result per file. How many files one request may carry is set by the plan (files per request).

fields.name: model
fields.description: "auto" (dynamically selected) or an explicit OpenRouter model id.

behavior.note: Any other value -> 400 ai_input_invalid.

fields.description: Inline text input.

fields.name: instructions
fields.description: Free-form instructions / generation prompt.

fields.name: labels
fields.description: (JSON-encoded array)

fields.name: presetId
fields.description: Apply a saved preset (create one with POST /v1/presets). Every value stored in the preset is used unless this request sets that field itself. The preset must have been saved for this same endpoint; requires an individual customer API key.

fields.name: app
fields.description: The name of the app that makes this call, for example "My shop importer". It is shown in your History next to the result, so you can tell which app did what. The official apps fill it in themselves (Davix H2I plugin, Davix H2I n8n node, Davix H2I Studio, Davix H2I Customer Portal); when you leave it out, the official SDKs and plugins are recognised from their User-Agent. Up to 60 characters; control characters and angle brackets are removed. The header `X-Davix-App` does the same. It is only a label: it never changes what the call does.

behavior.normalization: plain text, one line, cut to 60 characters; blank = not set

fields.name: source_url
fields.description: Fetch the input from this public http(s) address instead of uploading a file in "files". Send either the file or source_url, not both. Only public addresses on port 80/443 are fetched (never loopback, private, link-local or cloud-metadata addresses), redirects are re-checked, and the download is size- and time-limited; the fetched file is then judged exactly like an upload (content sniffing, format and size limits).

behavior.note: Not an http(s) URL, credentials in the URL, or an address that is not public -> 400 url_blocked; a download that fails, is too slow or redirects too often -> 400 url_fetch_failed; larger than the limit -> 413 file_too_large; a plan without URL input -> 403 format_not_allowed.

fields.name: source_urls
fields.description: A list of public http(s) addresses to fetch as inputs, as a JSON array, for example ["https://example.com/a.pdf","https://example.com/b.pdf"]. They are added to any files you upload: uploaded files come first, then the URLs, in the order sent. Together they cannot exceed the files-per-request limit of your plan. Only public addresses on port 80/443 are fetched (never loopback, private, link-local or cloud-metadata addresses), redirects are re-checked, and the download is size- and time-limited; every fetched file is then judged exactly like an upload (content sniffing, format and size limits).

behavior.note: Not an http(s) URL, credentials in the URL, or an address that is not public -> 400 url_blocked; a download that fails, is too slow or redirects too often -> 400 url_fetch_failed; larger than the limit -> 413 file_too_large; a plan without URL input -> 403 format_not_allowed; a file and a URL for the same input -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: async
fields.description: Opt-in asynchronous execution. With async=true and an individual customer API key the endpoint answers 202 {job_id, status_url} and the result becomes available from GET /v1/jobs/{id}. Omitted/false = the normal synchronous response. All the files of the request belong to one job; the AI answer envelope is the job result (GET /v1/jobs/{id}). Studio never sends it: this is for API calls.

behavior.normalization: only boolean true or the string "true" enables it
behavior.note: With any other key type the request is rejected with 400 async_requires_customer_key.

response.description: The Davix H2I AI response envelope.

Only public addresses on port 80/443 are fetched (never loopback, private, link-local or cloud-metadata addresses), redirects are re-checked, and the download is size- and time-limited; the fetched file is then judged exactly like an upload (content sniffing, format and size limits).

behavior.note: Not an http(s) URL, credentials in the URL, or an address that is not public -> 400 url_blocked; a download that fails, is too slow or redirects too often -> 400 url_fetch_failed; larger than the limit -> 413 file_too_large; a plan without URL input -> 403 format_not_allowed.

fields.name: source_urls
fields.description: A list of public http(s) addresses to fetch as inputs, as a JSON array, for example ["https://example.com/a.pdf","https://example.com/b.pdf"]. They are added to any files you upload: uploaded files come first, then the URLs, in the order sent. Together they cannot exceed the files-per-request limit of your plan. Only public addresses on port 80/443 are fetched (never loopback, private, link-local or cloud-metadata addresses), redirects are re-checked, and the download is size- and time-limited; every fetched file is then judged exactly like an upload (content sniffing, format and size limits).

behavior.note: Not an http(s) URL, credentials in the URL, or an address that is not public -> 400 url_blocked; a download that fails, is too slow or redirects too often -> 400 url_fetch_failed; larger than the limit -> 413 file_too_large; a plan without URL input -> 403 format_not_allowed; a file and a URL for the same input -> 400 invalid_parameter.

endpoints.name: AI colorization
endpoints.description:
Colorize black-and-white photos. **Currently returns 501 feature_unavailable**: No dedicated image-enhancement model is available through the provider, and general image-generation models regenerate pixels rather than faithfully enhancing them. The feature is enabled only after a model passes the fidelity benchmark.

Classification: ai. Deterministic stages: upload content sniffing, input normalisation (Sharp), output validation (Sharp), fidelity check against the input (Sharp).

fields.name: files
fields.description: Image file(s): PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, TIFF, AVIF, SVG, BMP, ICO, PNM, TGA, DDS, PSD, JPEG XL, JPEG 2000, EPS/AI/PS. Type is detected from content; non-raster formats are converted to PNG before the model sees them. Max 1.

file.note: The operation handles one file per run; send several files in this field and each is processed on its own, answered as one result per file. How many files one request may carry is set by the plan (files per request).

fields.description: Apply a saved preset (create one with POST /v1/presets). Every value stored in the preset is used unless this request sets that field itself. The preset must have been saved for this same endpoint; requires an individual customer API key.

fields.name: response
fields.description: How the result comes back. url (default) = the usual JSON answer with a signed URL per file. binary = the file itself as the HTTP body with Content-Type and Content-Disposition (a request with several result files returns one zip). base64 = the JSON answer with each result carrying `data` (base64) and `mimeType` instead of `url`, up to 20 MB in total. Answers without a result file are returned as JSON either way. Not available together with `async: true`.

behavior.normalization: lower-cased
behavior.note: Any other value -> 400 invalid_parameter. Combined with async: true (binary / base64) -> 400 invalid_parameter. Results above 300 MB (binary, several files) or 20 MB (base64) are not inlined: the JSON answer lists the files as usual and carries response_error / base64_error.

fields.name: filename
fields.description: The name for the result file (without extension; the extension follows the format). Used as the download name: Content-Disposition for response=binary, `downloadName` in the JSON answer otherwise. Path separators, control and bidirectional characters and Windows-reserved characters are removed; names are capped at 150 bytes. Several result files get -1, -2 ... added.

behavior.normalization: sanitised (never rejected for its characters); longer than 255 characters -> 400 invalid_parameter; together with filename_template -> 400 invalid_parameter

fields.name: filename_template
fields.description: A name built per result file from placeholders: {name} (the input file name without extension), {index} (1, 2, ...), {date} (YYYY-MM-DD), {time} (HH-MM-SS, UTC), {format} (the result extension) and {operation}. Example: "{name}-{index}-{date}". Sanitised like filename; result files that would get the same name are numbered -2, -3 ... Not together with filename.

behavior.note: An unknown placeholder or an unmatched brace -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: output_bundle
fields.description: zip = return the result files of this request as ONE zip download (`bundle.url`) instead of one signed URL per file. It applies when the request produces two or more files (several input files, or an operation with several outputs); with a single result file the normal answer is returned. The files in `results` then carry `bundleEntry` (their place in the zip) instead of `url`. Not available together with `async: true`.

behavior.note: Any value other than zip -> 400 invalid_parameter. Combined with async: true -> 400 invalid_parameter. Results above 300 MB in total are not bundled: the answer lists the files as usual and carries `bundle_error`.

fields.name: seed
fields.description: A number that asks the model to repeat a result: the same seed with the same request tends to give the same image. Only models that advertise a seed parameter take it. With on_unsupported=error (the default) a model without it is refused, or skipped when the model is chosen automatically; with on_unsupported=ignore the request runs and a warning says the seed was not applied. Providers do not guarantee identical images.

behavior.note: Not a whole number, negative or above 2147483647 -> 400 ai_input_invalid.

The official apps fill it in themselves (Davix H2I plugin, Davix H2I n8n node, Davix H2I Studio, Davix H2I Customer Portal); when you leave it out, the official SDKs and plugins are recognised from their User-Agent. Up to 60 characters; control characters and angle brackets are removed. The header `X-Davix-App` does the same. It is only a label: it never changes what the call does.

behavior.normalization: plain text, one line, cut to 60 characters; blank = not set

fields.name: source_url
fields.description: Fetch the input from this public http(s) address instead of uploading a file in "files". Send either the file or source_url, not both. Only public addresses on port 80/443 are fetched (never loopback, private, link-local or cloud-metadata addresses), redirects are re-checked, and the download is size- and time-limited; the fetched file is then judged exactly like an upload (content sniffing, format and size limits).

behavior.note: Not an http(s) URL, credentials in the URL, or an address that is not public -> 400 url_blocked; a download that fails, is too slow or redirects too often -> 400 url_fetch_failed; larger than the limit -> 413 file_too_large; a plan without URL input -> 403 format_not_allowed.

fields.name: async
fields.description: Opt-in asynchronous execution. With async=true and an individual customer API key the endpoint answers 202 {job_id, status_url} and the result becomes available from GET /v1/jobs/{id}. Omitted/false = the normal synchronous response. All the files of the request belong to one job; the AI answer envelope is the job result (GET /v1/jobs/{id}). Studio never sends it: this is for API calls.

behavior.normalization: only boolean true or the string "true" enables it
behavior.note: With any other key type the request is rejected with 400 async_requires_customer_key.

response.description: The Davix H2I AI response envelope.

endpoints.name: Generate (image)
endpoints.description:
Generic prompt-to-image (or image-to-image) generation with automatic or explicit model. Readiness: unbenchmarked (see GET /v1/ai/capabilities/core.generate).

Classification: ai. Deterministic stages: generated image validation and re-encoding (Sharp).

fields.name: files
fields.description: Image file(s): PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, TIFF, AVIF, SVG, BMP, ICO, PNM, TGA, DDS, PSD, JPEG XL, JPEG 2000, EPS/AI/PS. Type is detected from content; non-raster formats are converted to PNG before the model sees them. Max 1.

file.note: The operation handles one file per run; send several files in this field and each is processed on its own, answered as one result per file. How many files one request may carry is set by the plan (files per request).

fields.name: model
fields.description: "auto" (dynamically selected) or an explicit OpenRouter model id.

behavior.note: Any other value -> 400 ai_input_invalid.

fields.name: fallback
fields.description: Allow automatic fallback to another eligible model even when `model` is explicit.

fields.name: instructions
fields.description: Free-form instructions / generation prompt.

fields.name: presetId
fields.description: Apply a saved preset (create one with POST /v1/presets). Every value stored in the preset is used unless this request sets that field itself. The preset must have been saved for this same endpoint; requires an individual customer API key.

fields.name: response
fields.description: How the result comes back. url (default) = the usual JSON answer with a signed URL per file. binary = the file itself as the HTTP body with Content-Type and Content-Disposition (a request with several result files returns one zip). base64 = the JSON answer with each result carrying `data` (base64) and `mimeType` instead of `url`, up to 20 MB in total. Answers without a result file are returned as JSON either way. Not available together with `async: true`.

behavior.normalization: lower-cased
behavior.note: Any other value -> 400 invalid_parameter. Combined with async: true (binary / base64) -> 400 invalid_parameter. Results above 300 MB (binary, several files) or 20 MB (base64) are not inlined: the JSON answer lists the files as usual and carries response_error / base64_error.

fields.name: filename
fields.description: The name for the result file (without extension; the extension follows the format). Used as the download name: Content-Disposition for response=binary, `downloadName` in the JSON answer otherwise. behavior.normalization: sanitised (never rejected for its characters); longer than 255 characters -> 400 invalid_parameter; together with filename_template -> 400 invalid_parameter

fields.name: filename_template
fields.description: A name built per result file from placeholders: {name} (the input file name without extension), {index} (1, 2, ...), {date} (YYYY-MM-DD), {time} (HH-MM-SS, UTC), {format} (the result extension) and {operation}. Example: "{name}-{index}-{date}". Sanitised like filename; result files that would get the same name are numbered -2, -3 ... Not together with filename.

behavior.note: An unknown placeholder or an unmatched brace -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: output_bundle
fields.description: zip = return the result files of this request as ONE zip download (`bundle.url`) instead of one signed URL per file. It applies when the request produces two or more files (several input files, or an operation with several outputs); with a single result file the normal answer is returned. The files in `results` then carry `bundleEntry` (their place in the zip) instead of `url`. Not available together with `async: true`.

behavior.note: Any value other than zip -> 400 invalid_parameter. Combined with async: true -> 400 invalid_parameter. Results above 300 MB in total are not bundled: the answer lists the files as usual and carries `bundle_error`.

fields.name: seed
fields.description: A number that asks the model to repeat a result: the same seed with the same request tends to give the same image. Only models that advertise a seed parameter take it. With on_unsupported=error (the default) a model without it is refused, or skipped when the model is chosen automatically; with on_unsupported=ignore the request runs and a warning says the seed was not applied. Providers do not guarantee identical images.

behavior.note: Not a whole number, negative or above 2147483647 -> 400 ai_input_invalid.

Only public addresses on port 80/443 are fetched (never loopback, private, link-local or cloud-metadata addresses), redirects are re-checked, and the download is size- and time-limited; the fetched file is then judged exactly like an upload (content sniffing, format and size limits).

behavior.note: Not an http(s) URL, credentials in the URL, or an address that is not public -> 400 url_blocked; a download that fails, is too slow or redirects too often -> 400 url_fetch_failed; larger than the limit -> 413 file_too_large; a plan without URL input -> 403 format_not_allowed.

fields.name: async
fields.description: Opt-in asynchronous execution. With async=true and an individual customer API key the endpoint answers 202 {job_id, status_url} and the result becomes available from GET /v1/jobs/{id}. Omitted/false = the normal synchronous response. All the files of the request belong to one job; the AI answer envelope is the job result (GET /v1/jobs/{id}). Studio never sends it: this is for API calls.

behavior.normalization: only boolean true or the string "true" enables it
behavior.note: With any other key type the request is rejected with 400 async_requires_customer_key.

response.description: The Davix H2I AI response envelope.

endpoints.name: Convert between structured-data formats
endpoints.description: Convert CSV, TSV, JSON, NDJSON, XML, YAML, TOML, XLSX, ODS, HTML tables, Markdown tables, SQL dumps, SQLite and Parquet files into one another, with column / filter / sort / limit controls.

fields.name: file
fields.description: The source file.

file.note: Limits: at most 200,000 rows and 2,000 columns per sheet, 100 sheets; JSON/YAML nesting up to 50 levels; XML input up to 20 MB. The format is recognised from the file itself (its content, then its name); there is no source-format parameter. A file in an unsupported format -> 400 invalid_parameter naming the supported formats. The operation handles one file per run; send several files in this field and each is processed on its own, answered as one result per file. How many files one request may carry is set by the plan (files per request).

fields.name: to
fields.description: Target format (see GET /v1/formats?family=data for what the server can write; SQLite and Parquet are read-only).

behavior.normalization: lower-cased
behavior.note: A format the plan does not include -> 403 format_not_allowed.

fields.name: sheet
fields.description: Worksheet / table name to read or write (default: the first one). XLSX, ODS and XLS sheets, HTML and Markdown tables, SQL and SQLite tables.

behavior.note: Unknown name -> 400 (details.available lists the names).

fields.name: delimiter
fields.description: Field separator for CSV/TSV input and output: one character, or comma, semicolon, tab, pipe.

behavior.note: More than one character (or a quote / line break) -> 400.

fields.name: encoding
fields.description: Character encoding of CSV/TSV/text input and of CSV/TSV output, e.g. utf-8, utf-16le, iso-8859-1, windows-1252, shift_jis, gbk, big5, euc-kr. A byte order mark wins on input; without one a non-UTF-8 file is read as windows-1252 (reported in warnings).

behavior.note: Unknown encoding -> 400.

fields.name: header
fields.description: true (default): the first row of the input holds column names, and CSV/TSV/HTML/Markdown/XLSX output gets a header row. false: columns are named column1, column2 ...

fields.name: flatten
fields.description: true (default): nested JSON/XML/YAML objects become dotted columns (a.b.c) when written as a table; false keeps them as JSON text in one cell.

fields.name: pretty
fields.description: true (default): indent JSON output; false writes it compact.

fields.name: dateFormat
fields.description: How dates are written: iso (default), date, datetime, unix, excel, or a pattern made of YYYY MM DD HH mm ss and separators, e.g. DD/MM/YYYY.

behavior.note: Anything else -> 400.

fields.name: infer_types
fields.description: true (default): numbers and true/false in text formats (CSV, TSV, HTML, Markdown) become numbers and booleans; values with leading zeros or that would lose precision stay text. false keeps every cell as text.

fields.name: columns
fields.description: Keep only these columns, in this order (comma-separated or a JSON array). Applied after filter, sort and limit.

behavior.note: Unknown column -> 400 (details.available).

fields.name: filter
fields.description: Keep only rows matching a condition: JSON like {"column":"age","op":"gte","value":18}, an array (all must match), or {"and":[...]} / {"or":[...]} / {"not":{...}}. Operators: eq ne gt gte lt lte in nin contains startswith endswith like empty notempty.

behavior.note: No regular expressions or code: only these operators.

fields.name: sort
fields.description: Sort rows: comma-separated columns, each optionally :asc or :desc (e.g. "country,age:desc"). Empty values sort last.

fields.name: limit
fields.description: Keep only the first N rows (after filter and sort).

fields.name: formula_safe
fields.description: true: prefix CSV/TSV cells that a spreadsheet would run as a formula (= + - @) with an apostrophe.

fields.name: rootName
fields.description: XML output: the root element name (default rows for tables). Invalid characters are replaced.

fields.name: rowName
fields.description: XML output: the element used for each row (default row).

fields.name: table
fields.description: SQL output: table name (default: the sheet name). SQLite input: read only this table (default: all tables).

fields.name: output_bundle
fields.description: zip = return the result files of this request as ONE zip download (`bundle.url`) instead of one signed URL per file. It applies when the request produces two or more files (several input files, or an operation with several outputs); with a single result file the normal answer is returned. The files in `results` then carry `bundleEntry` (their place in the zip) instead of `url`. Not available together with `async: true`.

behavior.note: Any value other than zip -> 400 invalid_parameter. Combined with async: true -> 400 invalid_parameter. Results above 300 MB in total are not bundled: the answer lists the files as usual and carries `bundle_error`.

fields.name: validate_only
fields.description: true = check the request without running it. The answer is `{ validated: true, valid, errors[], files, estimate, limits }` instead of the endpoint's usual answer: `errors` lists every parameter or file the real call would reject, `estimate` is what it would count against your plan, and `limits` are the limits that apply to this endpoint for your key. Nothing is processed, no files are produced and no files are counted against the plan; the call itself counts as one request. It does not run the operation, so a problem that only shows while processing (a crop outside the image, an unreadable file) is not found.

behavior.normalization: only "true" enables it

fields.name: presetId
fields.description: Apply a saved preset (create one with POST /v1/presets). Every value stored in the preset is used unless this request sets that field itself. The preset must have been saved for this same endpoint; requires an individual customer API key.

fields.name: response
fields.description: How the result comes back. url (default) = the usual JSON answer with a signed URL per file. binary = the file itself as the HTTP body with Content-Type and Content-Disposition (a request with several result files returns one zip). base64 = the JSON answer with each result carrying `data` (base64) and `mimeType` instead of `url`, up to 20 MB in total. Answers without a result file are returned as JSON either way. Not available together with `async: true`.

behavior.normalization: lower-cased
behavior.note: Any other value -> 400 invalid_parameter. Combined with async: true (binary / base64) -> 400 invalid_parameter. Results above 300 MB (binary, several files) or 20 MB (base64) are not inlined: the JSON answer lists the files as usual and carries response_error / base64_error.

fields.name: filename
fields.description: The name for the result file (without extension; the extension follows the format). Used as the download name: Content-Disposition for response=binary, `downloadName` in the JSON answer otherwise. Path separators, control and bidirectional characters and Windows-reserved characters are removed; names are capped at 150 bytes. Several result files get -1, -2 ... added.

behavior.normalization: sanitised (never rejected for its characters); longer than 255 characters -> 400 invalid_parameter; together with filename_template -> 400 invalid_parameter

fields.name: filename_template
fields.description: A name built per result file from placeholders: {name} (the input file name without extension), {index} (1, 2, ...), {date} (YYYY-MM-DD), {time} (HH-MM-SS, UTC), {format} (the result extension) and {operation}. Example: "{name}-{index}-{date}". Sanitised like filename; result files that would get the same name are numbered -2, -3 ... Not together with filename.

behavior.note: An unknown placeholder or an unmatched brace -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: app
fields.description: The name of the app that makes this call, for example "My shop importer". It is shown in your History next to the result, so you can tell which app did what. The official apps fill it in themselves (Davix H2I plugin, Davix H2I n8n node, Davix H2I Studio, Davix H2I Customer Portal); when you leave it out, the official SDKs and plugins are recognised from their User-Agent. Up to 60 characters; control characters and angle brackets are removed. The header `X-Davix-App` does the same. It is only a label: it never changes what the call does.

behavior.normalization: plain text, one line, cut to 60 characters; blank = not set

fields.name: source_url
fields.description: Fetch the input from this public http(s) address instead of uploading a file in "file". Send either the file or source_url, not both. Only public addresses on port 80/443 are fetched (never loopback, private, link-local or cloud-metadata addresses), redirects are re-checked, and the download is size- and time-limited; the fetched file is then judged exactly like an upload (content sniffing, format and size limits).

behavior.note: Not an http(s) URL, credentials in the URL, or an address that is not public -> 400 url_blocked; a download that fails, is too slow or redirects too often -> 400 url_fetch_failed; larger than the limit -> 413 file_too_large; a plan without URL input -> 403 format_not_allowed.

fields.name: source_urls
fields.description: A list of public http(s) addresses to fetch as inputs, as a JSON array, for example ["https://example.com/a.pdf","https://example.com/b.pdf"]. They are added to any files you upload: uploaded files come first, then the URLs, in the order sent. Together they cannot exceed the files-per-request limit of your plan. Only public addresses on port 80/443 are fetched (never loopback, private, link-local or cloud-metadata addresses), redirects are re-checked, and the download is size- and time-limited; every fetched file is then judged exactly like an upload (content sniffing, format and size limits).

behavior.note: Not an http(s) URL, credentials in the URL, or an address that is not public -> 400 url_blocked; a download that fails, is too slow or redirects too often -> 400 url_fetch_failed; larger than the limit -> 413 file_too_large; a plan without URL input -> 403 format_not_allowed; a file and a URL for the same input -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: Idempotency-Key
fields.description: Optional idempotency key (8-128 characters). Reuse it for a retry of the SAME request; a different request with the same key -> 409 idempotency_key_conflict.

fields.name: async
fields.description: Opt-in asynchronous execution. With async=true and an individual customer API key the endpoint answers 202 {job_id, status_url} and the result becomes available from GET /v1/jobs/{id}. Omitted/false = the normal synchronous response. A request that carries several files in one field is not run as a job: it is processed immediately, answered with one result per file, and a `warnings` entry says that async was not applied.

behavior.normalization: only boolean true or the string "true" enables it
behavior.note: With any other key type the request is rejected with 400 async_requires_customer_key.

response.description: For to=json: {data: <parsed JSON>} inline. For to=csv/xlsx/xml: {url, sizeBytes} -- a signed download URL, matching every other file-producing endpoint in this API.

warnings.description: What the conversion had to do: flattened keys, a fallback encoding, sheets that were not written ...
What the conversion had to do: flattened keys, a fallback encoding, sheets that were not written ...

schema.description: to=json -> {data}; every other target -> {url,sizeBytes} of the converted file.

endpoints.notes: to=json returns the parsed data inline ({data}); other targets return a signed download URL. `warnings` lists what the conversion had to do (flattened keys, a fallback encoding, a sheet that was not written). This endpoint does not support async jobs.

endpoints.name: Fill a DOCX / ODT template with data (mail merge)

fields.name: file
fields.description: The template (DOCX or ODT) with {{field}} placeholders. Placeholders may be split over formatting runs; headers, footers and footnotes are filled too. Send the file or the id of a saved template (templateId).

file.note: Macro-enabled Office files, binary Office files that contain macros or link other files, and RTF with external links / DDE are rejected (400). Size limits are plan/settings limits. The operation handles one file per run; send several files in this field and each is processed on its own, answered as one result per file. How many files one request may carry is set by the plan (files per request).

fields.name: templateId
fields.description: Merge a saved DOCX / ODT template instead of uploading a file (create one with POST /v1/templates/upload). Fill it with `data` (one document), `records` or `data_file`; a default of the template fills what a record leaves empty and a required variable that stays empty is refused. Send templateId or file, not both. Requires an individual customer API key.

behavior.note: Unknown, someone else's or wrong-kind template -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: data_file
fields.description: Records as a CSV, JSON, XLSX, TSV, YAML ... file: one document per row.

file.note: Send exactly one of records, data or data_file.

fields.name: records
fields.description: One object per document: [{"name":"Ada","city":"London"}, ...] (at most 200). How many records one request may carry, and how they count toward the quota, is set per plan.

fields.name: data
fields.description: One record, for a single document.

fields.name: to
fields.description: docx, odt or pdf (default: the template type).

fields.name: strict
fields.description: true: refuse the request when a placeholder has no value in some record (the answer lists them); false (default): such placeholders are left empty and listed in warnings.

fields.name: password
fields.description: Password of an encrypted template; used only to open it.

fields.name: validate_only
fields.description: true = check the request without running it. The answer is `{ validated: true, valid, errors[], files, estimate, limits }` instead of the endpoint's usual answer: `errors` lists every parameter or file the real call would reject, `estimate` is what it would count against your plan, and `limits` are the limits that apply to this endpoint for your key. Nothing is processed, no files are produced and no files are counted against the plan; the call itself counts as one request. It does not run the operation, so a problem that only shows while processing (a crop outside the image, an unreadable file) is not found.

behavior.normalization: only "true" enables it

fields.name: presetId
fields.description: Apply a saved preset (create one with POST /v1/presets). Every value stored in the preset is used unless this request sets that field itself. The preset must have been saved for this same endpoint; requires an individual customer API key.

fields.name: response
fields.description: How the result comes back. url (default) = the usual JSON answer with a signed URL per file. binary = the file itself as the HTTP body with Content-Type and Content-Disposition (a request with several result files returns one zip). base64 = the JSON answer with each result carrying `data` (base64) and `mimeType` instead of `url`, up to 20 MB in total. Answers without a result file are returned as JSON either way. Not available together with `async: true`.

behavior.normalization: lower-cased
behavior.note: Any other value -> 400 invalid_parameter. Combined with async: true (binary / base64) -> 400 invalid_parameter. Results above 300 MB (binary, several files) or 20 MB (base64) are not inlined: the JSON answer lists the files as usual and carries response_error / base64_error.

fields.name: filename
fields.description: The name for the result file (without extension; the extension follows the format). Used as the download name: Content-Disposition for response=binary, `downloadName` in the JSON answer otherwise. Path separators, control and bidirectional characters and Windows-reserved characters are removed; names are capped at 150 bytes. Several result files get -1, -2 ... added.

behavior.normalization: sanitised (never rejected for its characters); longer than 255 characters -> 400 invalid_parameter; together with filename_template -> 400 invalid_parameter

fields.name: filename_template
fields.description: A name built per result file from placeholders: {name} (the input file name without extension), {index} (1, 2, ...), {date} (YYYY-MM-DD), {time} (HH-MM-SS, UTC), {format} (the result extension) and {operation}. Example: "{name}-{index}-{date}". Sanitised like filename; result files that would get the same name are numbered -2, -3 ... Not together with filename.

behavior.note: An unknown placeholder or an unmatched brace -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: output_bundle
fields.description: zip = return the result files of this request as ONE zip download (`bundle.url`) instead of one signed URL per file. It applies when the request produces two or more files (several input files, or an operation with several outputs); with a single result file the normal answer is returned. The files in `results` then carry `bundleEntry` (their place in the zip) instead of `url`. Not available together with `async: true`.

behavior.note: Any value other than zip -> 400 invalid_parameter. Combined with async: true -> 400 invalid_parameter. Results above 300 MB in total are not bundled: the answer lists the files as usual and carries `bundle_error`.

fields.name: app
fields.description: The name of the app that makes this call, for example "My shop importer". It is shown in your History next to the result, so you can tell which app did what. The official apps fill it in themselves (Davix H2I plugin, Davix H2I n8n node, Davix H2I Studio, Davix H2I Customer Portal); when you leave it out, the official SDKs and plugins are recognised from their User-Agent. Up to 60 characters; control characters and angle brackets are removed. The header `X-Davix-App` does the same. It is only a label: it never changes what the call does.

behavior.normalization: plain text, one line, cut to 60 characters; blank = not set

fields.name: source_url
fields.description: Fetch the input from this public http(s) address instead of uploading a file in "file". Send either the file or source_url, not both. They are added to any files you upload: uploaded files come first, then the URLs, in the order sent. Together they cannot exceed the files-per-request limit of your plan. Only public addresses on port 80/443 are fetched (never loopback, private, link-local or cloud-metadata addresses), redirects are re-checked, and the download is size- and time-limited; every fetched file is then judged exactly like an upload (content sniffing, format and size limits).

behavior.note: Not an http(s) URL, credentials in the URL, or an address that is not public -> 400 url_blocked; a download that fails, is too slow or redirects too often -> 400 url_fetch_failed; larger than the limit -> 413 file_too_large; a plan without URL input -> 403 format_not_allowed; a file and a URL for the same input -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: Idempotency-Key
fields.description: Optional idempotency key (8-128 characters). Reuse it for a retry of the SAME request; a different request with the same key -> 409 idempotency_key_conflict.

fields.name: async
fields.description: Opt-in asynchronous execution. With async=true and an individual customer API key the endpoint answers 202 {job_id, status_url} and the result becomes available from GET /v1/jobs/{id}. Omitted/false = the normal synchronous response. A request that carries several files in one field is not run as a job: it is processed immediately, answered with one result per file, and a `warnings` entry says that async was not applied.

behavior.normalization: only boolean true or the string "true" enables it
behavior.note: With any other key type the request is rejected with 400 async_requires_customer_key.

response.description: { pages, results: [{ url, format, sizeBytes, width, height, pageNumber }], warnings? }

endpoints.name: Extract the text of a document
endpoints.description: The text of any supported document as plain text, Markdown or a structured JSON view (headings, paragraphs, lists, tables; pages for PDFs and presentations).

fields.name: file
fields.description: The document.

file.note: Accepted source types (detected from content): pdf, docx, odt, rtf, doc, xlsx, ods, xls, pptx, ppsx, odp, ppt, pps, odg, wpd (WordPerfect), wps (Works word processor), vsd, vsdx (Visio), html, txt, md, epub; text sources (html, txt, md, tex, rst, mediawiki, fb2, adoc, eml, msg) are declared with `from`. Macro-enabled Office files, binary Office files that contain macros or link other files, and RTF with external links / DDE are rejected (400). Size limits are plan/settings limits. The format is recognised from the file itself (its content, then its name); there is no source-format parameter. A file in an unsupported format -> 400 invalid_parameter naming the supported formats. The operation handles one file per run; send several files in this field and each is processed on its own, answered as one result per file. How many files one request may carry is set by the plan (files per request).

fields.name: password
fields.description: Password of an encrypted Office file; used only to open it, never logged or stored.

fields.name: format
fields.description: txt (default): plain text; md: Markdown (word-processing documents, spreadsheets, HTML, Markdown, text); json: a structured view ({ blocks } or { pages }).

fields.name: output
fields.description: inline (default): the text is in the answer; url: the text is written to a file. Text over 5 MB is always returned as a file.

fields.name: validate_only
fields.description: true = check the request without running it. The answer is `{ validated: true, valid, errors[], files, estimate, limits }` instead of the endpoint's usual answer: `errors` lists every parameter or file the real call would reject, `estimate` is what it would count against your plan, and `limits` are the limits that apply to this endpoint for your key. Nothing is processed, no files are produced and no files are counted against the plan; the call itself counts as one request. It does not run the operation, so a problem that only shows while processing (a crop outside the image, an unreadable file) is not found.

behavior.normalization: only "true" enables it

fields.name: presetId
fields.description: Apply a saved preset (create one with POST /v1/presets). Every value stored in the preset is used unless this request sets that field itself. The preset must have been saved for this same endpoint; requires an individual customer API key.

fields.name: response
fields.description: How the result comes back. url (default) = the usual JSON answer with a signed URL per file. binary = the file itself as the HTTP body with Content-Type and Content-Disposition (a request with several result files returns one zip). base64 = the JSON answer with each result carrying `data` (base64) and `mimeType` instead of `url`, up to 20 MB in total. Answers without a result file are returned as JSON either way. Not available together with `async: true`.

behavior.normalization: lower-cased
behavior.note: Any other value -> 400 invalid_parameter. Combined with async: true (binary / base64) -> 400 invalid_parameter. Results above 300 MB (binary, several files) or 20 MB (base64) are not inlined: the JSON answer lists the files as usual and carries response_error / base64_error.

fields.name: filename
fields.description: The name for the result file (without extension; the extension follows the format). Used as the download name: Content-Disposition for response=binary, `downloadName` in the JSON answer otherwise. Path separators, control and bidirectional characters and Windows-reserved characters are removed; names are capped at 150 bytes. Several result files get -1, -2 ... added.

behavior.normalization: sanitised (never rejected for its characters); longer than 255 characters -> 400 invalid_parameter; together with filename_template -> 400 invalid_parameter

fields.name: filename_template
fields.description: A name built per result file from placeholders: {name} (the input file name without extension), {index} (1, 2, ...), {date} (YYYY-MM-DD), {time} (HH-MM-SS, UTC), {format} (the result extension) and {operation}. Example: "{name}-{index}-{date}". Sanitised like filename; result files that would get the same name are numbered -2, -3 ... Not together with filename.

behavior.note: An unknown placeholder or an unmatched brace -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: output_bundle
fields.description: zip = return the result files of this request as ONE zip download (`bundle.url`) instead of one signed URL per file. It applies when the request produces two or more files (several input files, or an operation with several outputs); with a single result file the normal answer is returned. The files in `results` then carry `bundleEntry` (their place in the zip) instead of `url`. Not available together with `async: true`.

behavior.note: Any value other than zip -> 400 invalid_parameter. Combined with async: true -> 400 invalid_parameter. Results above 300 MB in total are not bundled: the answer lists the files as usual and carries `bundle_error`.

fields.name: app
fields.description: The name of the app that makes this call, for example "My shop importer". It is shown in your History next to the result, so you can tell which app did what. The official apps fill it in themselves (Davix H2I plugin, Davix H2I n8n node, Davix H2I Studio, Davix H2I Customer Portal); when you leave it out, the official SDKs and plugins are recognised from their User-Agent. endpoints.name: The file formats the API reads and writes, and which endpoint takes each
endpoints.description: Every format Davix H2I knows (images, documents, data): its MIME types and extensions, what it can do (read, write, animated, alpha, ...), which endpoints accept it as an upload (`accepted_by`) or produce it as a result (`produced_by`), whether the tool behind it is installed on this server (`available`), and whether the calling key's plan allows it (`allowed`). fields.description: Only formats of this family.

behavior.normalization: lower-cased

fields.name: direction
fields.description: input = formats the API can read; output = formats it can write.

behavior.normalization: lower-cased

fields.name: endpoint
fields.description: Only the formats this endpoint (its id, such as images.resize, or its path) accepts or produces.

behavior.note: An endpoint that declares no formats -> 404 not_found.

fields.name: status
fields.description: supported (default) lists what works today; planned lists formats that are recognised but not yet accepted; all lists both.

behavior.normalization: lower-cased

sets.description: Named format sets (for example image.input, image.output) -> format ids.

tools.description: Optional tools behind some formats -> { available, version }.

ocr.description: OCR languages installed on this server.

fonts.description: Installed font families and which writing systems this server can draw (every probed script, CJK and emoji are covered when listed as supported).

endpoints.notes: Plan-aware: for a customer key `allowed` reflects the plan's format switches (allow_fmt_<group>) on each endpoint. The registry is code, not data; a format only becomes `supported` together with the test that proves it.

endpoints.name: Generate a barcode
endpoints.description: A barcode as PNG, SVG or PDF. Symbologies: code128 (Code 128: any ASCII text); code39 (Code 39: A-Z 0-9 - . $ / + % space); ean13 (EAN-13: 12 digits (the check digit is added) or 13); ean8 (EAN-8: 7 digits (the check digit is added) or 8); upca (UPC-A: 11 digits (the check digit is added) or 12); itf (Interleaved 2 of 5: an even number of digits); codabar (Codabar: digits and - $ : / . + between start/stop letters A-D); datamatrix (Data Matrix: any text); pdf417 (PDF417: any text); aztec (Aztec: any text); qrcode (QR Code (barcode renderer): any text). Each one is proven by generating it and reading it back. Counts as one file.

fields.name: symbology
fields.description: The barcode type: code128 (Code 128: any ASCII text); code39 (Code 39: A-Z 0-9 - . $ / + % space); ean13 (EAN-13: 12 digits (the check digit is added) or 13); ean8 (EAN-8: 7 digits (the check digit is added) or 8); upca (UPC-A: 11 digits (the check digit is added) or 12); itf (Interleaved 2 of 5: an even number of digits); codabar (Codabar: digits and - $ : / . + between start/stop letters A-D); datamatrix (Data Matrix: any text); pdf417 (PDF417: any text); aztec (Aztec: any text); qrcode (QR Code (barcode renderer): any text).

fields.name: text
fields.description: What the barcode holds. Each symbology accepts different characters (see symbology); a refusal says what is expected. EAN / UPC check digits are added when you send one digit fewer.

fields.name: file_type
fields.description: png (default), svg or pdf.

fields.name: color
fields.description: Foreground colour, e.g. #000000 (default).

fields.name: background
fields.description: Background colour, e.g. #ffffff (default).

fields.name: scale
fields.description: Size of one module in pixels: 1 to 10, default 3 (PDF uses at least 6).

fields.name: height
fields.description: Bar height in millimetres for linear codes and the row height of PDF417: 3 to 200, default 10. Square codes (Data Matrix, Aztec, QR) keep their shape.

fields.name: include_text
fields.description: Print the human readable text under linear codes.

fields.name: padding
fields.description: Quiet zone around the code in pixels: 0 to 100, default 10.

fields.name: rotate
fields.description: N (default), R (90 degrees), L (270) or I (180).

fields.name: validate_only
fields.description: true = check the request without running it. The answer is `{ validated: true, valid, errors[], files, estimate, limits }` instead of the endpoint's usual answer: `errors` lists every parameter or file the real call would reject, `estimate` is what it would count against your plan, and `limits` are the limits that apply to this endpoint for your key. Nothing is processed, no files are produced and no files are counted against the plan; the call itself counts as one request. It does not run the operation, so a problem that only shows while processing (a crop outside the image, an unreadable file) is not found.

behavior.normalization: only "true" enables it

fields.name: presetId
fields.description: Apply a saved preset (create one with POST /v1/presets). Every value stored in the preset is used unless this request sets that field itself. The preset must have been saved for this same endpoint; requires an individual customer API key.

fields.name: response
fields.description: How the result comes back. url (default) = the usual JSON answer with a signed URL per file. binary = the file itself as the HTTP body with Content-Type and Content-Disposition (a request with several result files returns one zip). base64 = the JSON answer with each result carrying `data` (base64) and `mimeType` instead of `url`, up to 20 MB in total. Answers without a result file are returned as JSON either way. Not available together with `async: true`.

behavior.normalization: lower-cased
behavior.note: Any other value -> 400 invalid_parameter. Combined with async: true (binary / base64) -> 400 invalid_parameter. Results above 300 MB (binary, several files) or 20 MB (base64) are not inlined: the JSON answer lists the files as usual and carries response_error / base64_error.

fields.name: filename
fields.description: The name for the result file (without extension; the extension follows the format). Used as the download name: Content-Disposition for response=binary, `downloadName` in the JSON answer otherwise. Path separators, control and bidirectional characters and Windows-reserved characters are removed; names are capped at 150 bytes. Several result files get -1, -2 ... added.

behavior.normalization: sanitised (never rejected for its characters); longer than 255 characters -> 400 invalid_parameter; together with filename_template -> 400 invalid_parameter

fields.name: filename_template
fields.description: A name built per result file from placeholders: {name} (the input file name without extension), {index} (1, 2, ...), {date} (YYYY-MM-DD), {time} (HH-MM-SS, UTC), {format} (the result extension) and {operation}. Example: "{name}-{index}-{date}". Sanitised like filename; result files that would get the same name are numbered -2, -3 ... Not together with filename.

behavior.note: An unknown placeholder or an unmatched brace -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: app
fields.description: The name of the app that makes this call, for example "My shop importer". It is shown in your History next to the result, so you can tell which app did what. The official apps fill it in themselves (Davix H2I plugin, Davix H2I n8n node, Davix H2I Studio, Davix H2I Customer Portal); when you leave it out, the official SDKs and plugins are recognised from their User-Agent. Up to 60 characters; control characters and angle brackets are removed. The header `X-Davix-App` does the same. It is only a label: it never changes what the call does.

behavior.normalization: plain text, one line, cut to 60 characters; blank = not set

fields.name: Idempotency-Key
fields.description: Optional idempotency key (8-128 characters). Reuse it for a retry of the SAME request; a different request with the same key -> 409 idempotency_key_conflict.

fields.name: async
fields.description: Opt-in asynchronous execution. With async=true and an individual customer API key the endpoint answers 202 {job_id, status_url} and the result becomes available from GET /v1/jobs/{id}. Omitted/false = the normal synchronous response. A request that carries several files in one field is not run as a job: it is processed immediately, answered with one result per file, and a `warnings` entry says that async was not applied.

behavior.normalization: only boolean true or the string "true" enables it
behavior.note: With any other key type the request is rejected with 400 async_requires_customer_key.

response.description: { results: [{ url, format, sizeBytes, width, height, symbology }] }

endpoints.name: Compare two images
endpoints.description: How different are two images, and where? Reports the share of differing pixels (anti-aliasing aware), structural similarity (SSIM), a perceptual-hash distance and PSNR, can limit the comparison to a region or break the difference down per grid cell, and returns a diff image that paints what changed. Images of different sizes are scaled to each other first (`resize_to`). `match` tells whether the difference stays within `max_diff_ratio`.

fields.name: imageA
fields.description: The first (reference) image to compare.

fields.name: imageB
fields.description: The second image to compare.

fields.name: metrics
fields.description: What to measure, comma separated: `pixel`, `ssim`, `hash`, `psnr`. Default `pixel,ssim,hash`.

behavior.note: An unknown metric -> 400 invalid_parameter with the allowed metrics.

fields.name: threshold
fields.description: Colour distance a pixel must exceed to count as different (0 = any change, 1 = nothing counts). Used by the pixel metric.

behavior.note: Outside 0-1 -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: include_aa
fields.description: true = count anti-aliased edge pixels as differences too (by default they are ignored).

behavior.note: Anything but true/false -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: alpha
fields.description: Opacity of the unchanged pixels in the diff image (0-1).

behavior.note: Outside 0-1 -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: diff_color
fields.description: Colour that paints differing pixels in the diff image. Default red.

behavior.note: Not a colour -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: max_diff_ratio
fields.description: The share of differing pixels (0-1) that still counts as a match. 0 = the images must be pixel-identical (at the threshold).

behavior.note: Outside 0-1 -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: resize_to
fields.description: How to handle different sizes: `a` (default) scales B to A's size, `b` scales A to B's, `none` refuses images of different sizes.

behavior.normalization: lower-cased
behavior.note: Any other value -> 400 invalid_parameter; `none` with different sizes -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: region
fields.description: Compare only this rectangle (in the images' pixels, after resizing): {"x":0,"y":0,"width":200,"height":100}.

behavior.note: Not valid JSON, missing a key, or outside the image -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: grid
fields.description: Also report the difference of every cell of a COLUMNSxROWS grid, e.g. `4x4` (up to 32x32): where the images differ. Needs the pixel metric.

behavior.note: Not COLUMNSxROWS or larger than 32x32 -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: diff_image
fields.description: true (default) = return a PNG that paints the differing pixels (`results[0]`). false = numbers only.

behavior.note: Anything but true/false -> 400 invalid_parameter.

endpoints.name: Composite multiple image/text/color layers onto a base image

fields.name: images
fields.description: images[0] is the base image; any further files can be referenced by layers[].imageIndex.

file.note: Accepted types are enforced per upload (the formats registry, set image.input); the number of files and total size are plan/settings limits (runtime), not static contract limits.

fields.name: layers
fields.description: Ordered layers (JSON array, max 10).

properties.name: type
properties.description: Layer kind: image (an uploaded picture), text, color (a solid rectangle) or gradient.

behavior.normalization: lower-cased

properties.name: imageIndex
properties.description: For type=image: 1-based index into the uploaded images AFTER the base (the base is always images[0]).

behavior.normalization: lower-cased

behavior.note: Outside the range -> 0 (not clamped).
Clamped to [0,1]; non-numeric -> 1.

properties.name: scale
properties.description: For type=image: size as a fraction of the smaller base dimension.

behavior.note: Clamped to [0.01,1].

properties.name: color
properties.description: Text color (default #ffffff) or fill color for type=color (default #000000).

properties.name: width
properties.description: For type=color: rectangle width (px); default 20% of the base width.

behavior.note: Outside [1, base width] -> default.

properties.name: height
properties.description: For type=color: rectangle height (px); default 20% of the base height.

properties.name: underlay
properties.description: Composite the layer under the base image.

behavior.normalization: true or "true"

properties.name: angle
properties.description: For a linear gradient: direction in degrees (0 = left to right, 90 = top to bottom).

properties.name: mask
properties.description: Mask this layer with an uploaded image (white keeps, black hides).

properties.name: imageIndex
properties.description: Which uploaded image (after the base) is the mask: its brightness becomes the layer's opacity.

properties.name: invert
properties.description: true = black keeps and white hides.

behavior.note: An imageIndex that does not reference an uploaded image after the base -> 400 invalid_parameter.

properties.name: fontFamily
properties.description: Font family (GET /v1/formats lists the installed ones) or a generic name: sans-serif (default), serif, monospace, emoji. Characters the font lacks are drawn from a fallback font that has them (every script, CJK and emoji).

behavior.note: A family that is not installed -> 400 font_unavailable.

properties.name: fontWeight
properties.description: Weight: thin, light, normal (default), medium, semibold, bold, heavy, or a number 100-900.

behavior.note: Anything else -> 400 invalid_parameter.

properties.name: italic
properties.description: true = italic (a synthetic slant if the font has none).

properties.name: align
properties.description: Alignment of wrapped lines: left (default), center, right.

behavior.note: Any other value -> 400 invalid_parameter.

properties.name: direction
properties.description: Base text direction: auto (default, from the text), ltr or rtl.

behavior.note: Any other value -> 400 invalid_parameter.

properties.name: lang
properties.description: Language of the text (ja, ko, zh-CN, zh-TW, ar, fa, ...): chooses the right regional form of Han characters and the right Arabic-script face.

behavior.note: Not a language tag -> 400 invalid_parameter.

properties.name: letterSpacing
properties.description: Extra space between characters in pixels (-10 to 100).

properties.name: lineSpacing
properties.description: Line height multiplier for wrapped text (0.5 to 4, default 1).

behavior.note: Empty or more than 10 layers -> 400. A layer entirely outside the base -> 400.
