fields.name: quality
fields.description: Quality of lossy output (JPEG, WebP, AVIF; for TIFF it switches to JPEG compression). With only `quality` the result keeps its own format and is re-encoded at this quality. PNG and GIF are lossless and ignore it.

behavior.note: Outside 1-100 or not a whole number -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: lossless
fields.description: true = lossless WebP / AVIF (larger files, pixel-exact).

behavior.note: Anything but true/false -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: dpi
fields.description: Pixel density written into the result (PNG, JPEG, TIFF, BMP). It does not resample the image; for SVG input it also sets the resolution the vector is drawn at.

behavior.note: Outside 1-1200 -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.description: Colour handling of the result: srgb, grayscale, or cmyk (JPEG and TIFF only).

behavior.normalization: lower-cased

behavior.normalization: lower-cased
behavior.note: Any other value -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.description: Colour that replaces transparency when the result format cannot hold it (JPEG, BMP). Default white.

fields.description: With metadata=set: the author (EXIF Artist).

behavior.note: Control characters or more than 1024 characters -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.description: With metadata=set: the copyright notice (EXIF Copyright).

behavior.note: Control characters or more than 1024 characters -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: description
fields.description: With metadata=set: a description (EXIF ImageDescription).

behavior.note: Outside -180..180, or sent without gps_latitude -> 400 invalid_parameter.

endpoints.name: Build a photography-style contact sheet of thumbnails (feature-expansion phase, NEW)

fields.name: images
fields.description: Images (1-100).

file.note: 1-100 images (MAX_LAYOUT_IMAGES). Accepted types are enforced per upload; plan limits apply.

fields.name: cols
fields.description: Columns.

behavior.note: Math.max(1, parseInt(cols)); non-numeric -> automatic (ceil(sqrt(n))). No upper bound besides the 100-image and pixel limits.

fields.name: thumbSize
fields.description: Square thumbnail size (px).

behavior.note: Whole number of pixels, at least 1. Empty -> 150. Non-numeric, 0 or negative -> 400 invalid_parameter. A sheet above the plan's result-size limits -> 400 invalid_parameter.

dynamicLimit.description: The largest result a request may ask for is set per plan and per endpoint (max_output_dimension_px, max_output_pixels) and can be changed at any time; a larger request is 400 invalid_parameter with the limit in details.limit and details.limit_name. Read the limit that applies to your key from GET /v1/limits.

fields.name: spacing
fields.description: Gap between thumbnails (px).

behavior.note: Whole number of pixels from 0 to 500; anything else -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: background
fields.description: Sheet / letterbox background (hex, optionally with alpha).

behavior.note: Any CSS colour Sharp can parse (names, #rgb, #rrggbb, #rrggbbaa, rgb()/rgba()). Empty -> the default colour. An unparseable value -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: output_bundle
fields.description: zip = return the result files of this request as ONE zip download (`bundle.url`) instead of one signed URL per file. It applies when the request produces two or more files (several input files, or an operation with several outputs); with a single result file the normal answer is returned. fields.name: validate_only
fields.description: true = check the request without running it. The answer is `{ validated: true, valid, errors[], files, estimate, limits }` instead of the endpoint's usual answer: `errors` lists every parameter or file the real call would reject, `estimate` is what it would count against your plan, and `limits` are the limits that apply to this endpoint for your key. Nothing is processed, no files are produced and no files are counted against the plan; the call itself counts as one request. It does not run the operation, so a problem that only shows while processing (a crop outside the image, an unreadable file) is not found.

behavior.normalization: only "true" enables it

fields.name: presetId
fields.description: Apply a saved preset (create one with POST /v1/presets). Every value stored in the preset is used unless this request sets that field itself. The preset must have been saved for this same endpoint; requires an individual customer API key.

fields.name: response
fields.description: How the result comes back. url (default) = the usual JSON answer with a signed URL per file. binary = the file itself as the HTTP body with Content-Type and Content-Disposition (a request with several result files returns one zip). base64 = the JSON answer with each result carrying `data` (base64) and `mimeType` instead of `url`, up to 20 MB in total. Answers without a result file are returned as JSON either way. Not available together with `async: true`.

behavior.normalization: lower-cased
behavior.note: Any other value -> 400 invalid_parameter. Combined with async: true (binary / base64) -> 400 invalid_parameter. Results above 300 MB (binary, several files) or 20 MB (base64) are not inlined: the JSON answer lists the files as usual and carries response_error / base64_error.

fields.name: filename
fields.description: The name for the result file (without extension; the extension follows the format). Used as the download name: Content-Disposition for response=binary, `downloadName` in the JSON answer otherwise. behavior.normalization: sanitised (never rejected for its characters); longer than 255 characters -> 400 invalid_parameter; together with filename_template -> 400 invalid_parameter

fields.name: filename_template
fields.description: A name built per result file from placeholders: {name} (the input file name without extension), {index} (1, 2, ...), {date} (YYYY-MM-DD), {time} (HH-MM-SS, UTC), {format} (the result extension) and {operation}. fields.name: app

behavior.normalization: plain text, one line, cut to 60 characters; blank = not set

fields.name: Idempotency-Key
fields.description: Optional idempotency key (8-128 characters). Reuse it for a retry of the SAME request; a different request with the same key -> 409 idempotency_key_conflict.

fields.name: async
fields.description: Opt-in asynchronous execution. Only public addresses on port 80/443 are fetched (never loopback, private, link-local or cloud-metadata addresses), redirects are re-checked, and the download is size- and time-limited; the fetched file is then judged exactly like an upload (content sniffing, format and size limits).

behavior.note: Not an http(s) URL, credentials in the URL, or an address that is not public -> 400 url_blocked; a download that fails, is too slow or redirects too often -> 400 url_fetch_failed; larger than the limit -> 413 file_too_large; a plan without URL input -> 403 format_not_allowed.

fields.name: source_urls
fields.description: A list of public http(s) addresses to fetch as inputs, as a JSON array, for example ["https://example.com/a.pdf","https://example.com/b.pdf"]. They are added to any files you upload: uploaded files come first, then the URLs, in the order sent. Together they cannot exceed the files-per-request limit of your plan. Only public addresses on port 80/443 are fetched (never loopback, private, link-local or cloud-metadata addresses), redirects are re-checked, and the download is size- and time-limited; every fetched file is then judged exactly like an upload (content sniffing, format and size limits).

behavior.note: Not an http(s) URL, credentials in the URL, or an address that is not public -> 400 url_blocked; a download that fails, is too slow or redirects too often -> 400 url_fetch_failed; larger than the limit -> 413 file_too_large; a plan without URL input -> 403 format_not_allowed; a file and a URL for the same input -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: Idempotency-Key
fields.description: Optional idempotency key (8-128 characters). Reuse it for a retry of the SAME request; a different request with the same key -> 409 idempotency_key_conflict.

fields.name: async
fields.description: Opt-in asynchronous execution. With async=true and an individual customer API key the endpoint answers 202 {job_id, status_url} and the result becomes available from GET /v1/jobs/{id}. Omitted/false = the normal synchronous response. A request that carries several files in one field is not run as a job: it is processed immediately, answered with one result per file, and a `warnings` entry says that async was not applied.

behavior.normalization: only boolean true or the string "true" enables it
behavior.note: With any other key type the request is rejected with 400 async_requires_customer_key.

fields.name: images
fields.description: Image(s) to convert.

file.note: Accepted types are enforced per upload (the formats registry, set image.input); the number of files and total size are plan/settings limits (runtime), not static contract limits.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: perImage = one PDF per image; combined = one PDF.

fields.name: pageSize
fields.description: Page size; auto fits the image.

behavior.normalization: lower-cased

fields.name: orientation
fields.description: Page orientation (a4/letter).

behavior.normalization: lower-cased

fields.name: margin
fields.description: Page margin (points).

fields.name: embedFormat
fields.description: Raster format embedded in the PDF ("jpg" = jpeg).

behavior.normalization: lower-cased

fields.name: embedQuality
fields.description: JPEG embed quality.

behavior.note: Whole number from 20 to 100; anything else -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: imageOptions
fields.description: Per-image overrides (JSON array, one entry per uploaded image; not more entries than images).

fields.name: output_bundle
fields.description: zip = return the result files of this request as ONE zip download (`bundle.url`) instead of one signed URL per file. It applies when the request produces two or more files (several input files, or an operation with several outputs); with a single result file the normal answer is returned. The files in `results` then carry `bundleEntry` (their place in the zip) instead of `url`. Not available together with `async: true`.

behavior.note: Any value other than zip -> 400 invalid_parameter. Combined with async: true -> 400 invalid_parameter. Results above 300 MB in total are not bundled: the answer lists the files as usual and carries `bundle_error`.

fields.name: validate_only
fields.description: true = check the request without running it. The answer is `{ validated: true, valid, errors[], files, estimate, limits }` instead of the endpoint's usual answer: `errors` lists every parameter or file the real call would reject, `estimate` is what it would count against your plan, and `limits` are the limits that apply to this endpoint for your key. Nothing is processed, no files are produced and no files are counted against the plan; the call itself counts as one request. It does not run the operation, so a problem that only shows while processing (a crop outside the image, an unreadable file) is not found.

behavior.normalization: only "true" enables it

fields.name: presetId
fields.description: Apply a saved preset (create one with POST /v1/presets). Every value stored in the preset is used unless this request sets that field itself. The preset must have been saved for this same endpoint; requires an individual customer API key.

fields.name: response
fields.description: How the result comes back. url (default) = the usual JSON answer with a signed URL per file. binary = the file itself as the HTTP body with Content-Type and Content-Disposition (a request with several result files returns one zip). base64 = the JSON answer with each result carrying `data` (base64) and `mimeType` instead of `url`, up to 20 MB in total. Answers without a result file are returned as JSON either way. Not available together with `async: true`.

behavior.normalization: lower-cased
behavior.note: Any other value -> 400 invalid_parameter. Combined with async: true (binary / base64) -> 400 invalid_parameter. Results above 300 MB (binary, several files) or 20 MB (base64) are not inlined: the JSON answer lists the files as usual and carries response_error / base64_error.

fields.name: filename
fields.description: The name for the result file (without extension; the extension follows the format). Used as the download name: Content-Disposition for response=binary, `downloadName` in the JSON answer otherwise. Path separators, control and bidirectional characters and Windows-reserved characters are removed; names are capped at 150 bytes. Several result files get -1, -2 ... added.

behavior.normalization: sanitised (never rejected for its characters); longer than 255 characters -> 400 invalid_parameter; together with filename_template -> 400 invalid_parameter

fields.name: filename_template
fields.description: A name built per result file from placeholders: {name} (the input file name without extension), {index} (1, 2, ...), {date} (YYYY-MM-DD), {time} (HH-MM-SS, UTC), {format} (the result extension) and {operation}. Example: "{name}-{index}-{date}". Sanitised like filename; result files that would get the same name are numbered -2, -3 ... Not together with filename.

behavior.note: An unknown placeholder or an unmatched brace -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: app
fields.description: The name of the app that makes this call, for example "My shop importer". It is shown in your History next to the result, so you can tell which app did what. fields.name: margin

endpoints.name: Remove a plain background
endpoints.description: Makes the background of each picture transparent when it is (nearly) one colour: product photos on white, logos, scans, green-screen shots. Local and deterministic, no model. `mode=edges` removes only background connected to the picture's border; `mode=all` removes every matching pixel (chroma key). The result is a transparent PNG by default (any format that holds transparency via `output_format`). Pictures with a busy or graded background cannot be cut out by colour: use the AI image-edit endpoint for those.

fields.name: images
fields.description: Picture(s) whose background to remove. Every file is processed with the same parameters.

fields.name: background_color
fields.description: `auto` (default) takes the colour most of the picture's border has; or give the colour to remove, e.g. `#ffffff` or `#00ff00`.

behavior.note: Not auto, a hex colour or a basic colour name -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: tolerance
fields.description: How far a pixel may differ from the background colour and still count as background (0 = exact match, 100 = very loose).

behavior.note: Outside 0-100 -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: edges: remove only background connected to the border. all: remove every pixel that matches (chroma key).

behavior.normalization: lower-cased
behavior.note: Any other value -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: feather
fields.description: Softens the cut-out edge by this many pixels (0 = hard edge).

behavior.note: Outside 0-20 -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: shrink
fields.description: Pulls the cut-out edge inward by this many pixels to remove a leftover halo of background colour.

behavior.note: Outside 0-20 -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: output_format
fields.description: Format of the result: one of the image formats the API can write (GET /v1/formats?direction=output&family=image lists them). Leave it out to keep this endpoint's usual behaviour (the result keeps the input's format).

behavior.normalization: lower-cased (jpg = jpeg)
behavior.note: Not a writable format -> 400 invalid_parameter with the allowed values. A format the plan does not include -> 403 format_not_allowed.

fields.name: quality
fields.description: Quality of lossy output (JPEG, WebP, AVIF; for TIFF it switches to JPEG compression). With only `quality` the result keeps its own format and is re-encoded at this quality. PNG and GIF are lossless and ignore it.

behavior.note: Outside 1-100 or not a whole number -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: lossless
fields.description: true = lossless WebP / AVIF (larger files, pixel-exact).

behavior.note: Anything but true/false -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: dpi
fields.description: Pixel density written into the result (PNG, JPEG, TIFF, BMP). It does not resample the image; for SVG input it also sets the resolution the vector is drawn at.

behavior.note: Outside 1-1200 -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: colorspace
fields.description: Colour handling of the result: srgb, grayscale, or cmyk (JPEG and TIFF only).

behavior.normalization: lower-cased
behavior.note: Any other value -> 400 invalid_parameter; cmyk with a format that cannot hold it -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: blend.opacity

behavior.normalization: lower-cased

behavior.note: Any other value -> 400 invalid_parameter; cmyk with a format that cannot hold it -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: icc_profile

behavior.normalization: lower-cased
behavior.note: Any other value -> 400 invalid_parameter.

behavior.note: Not a colour -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: author
fields.description: With metadata=set: the author (EXIF Artist).

behavior.note: Control characters or more than 1024 characters -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: copyright
fields.description: With metadata=set: the copyright notice (EXIF Copyright).

behavior.note: Control characters or more than 1024 characters -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: description
fields.description: With metadata=set: a description (EXIF ImageDescription).

behavior.note: Control characters or more than 1024 characters -> 400 invalid_parameter.

behavior.note: Outside -1000..100000, or sent without a position -> 400 invalid_parameter.

behavior.note: At least one of watermark.text or an uploaded watermarkImage is required (400 missing_field).

behavior.normalization: lower-cased
behavior.note: Invalid -> 400 invalid_parameter (validated at the route boundary).

clampInt(): values outside [0,5000] or non-integers fall back to 24 (they are NOT clamped to the nearest bound).

properties.name: scale
properties.description: Image-overlay size as a fraction of the smaller base dimension.

properties.name: blendMode
properties.description: How the watermark combines with the picture (multiply, screen, overlay, ...).

behavior.note: Unrecognized value -> 400 invalid_parameter.

properties.description: Rotate the watermark by this many degrees (clockwise). The rotated watermark is kept inside the picture.

behavior.note: Outside -360..360 or not a number -> 400 invalid_parameter.

properties.name: shadow

properties.name: fontWeight
properties.description: Weight: thin, light, normal (default), medium, semibold, bold, heavy, or a number 100-900.

behavior.note: Anything else -> 400 invalid_parameter.

properties.name: italic
properties.description: true = italic (a synthetic slant if the font has none).

properties.name: align
properties.description: Alignment of wrapped lines: left (default), center, right.

behavior.note: Any other value -> 400 invalid_parameter.

properties.name: direction
properties.description: Base text direction: auto (default, from the text), ltr or rtl.

behavior.note: Any other value -> 400 invalid_parameter.

properties.name: lang
properties.description: Language of the text (ja, ko, zh-CN, zh-TW, ar, fa, ...): chooses the right regional form of Han characters and the right Arabic-script face.

behavior.note: Not a language tag -> 400 invalid_parameter.

properties.name: letterSpacing
properties.description: Extra space between characters in pixels (-10 to 100).

behavior.note: Invalid JSON -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: watermarkImage
fields.description: Overlay image (one file).

endpoints.name: OCR scanned PDFs to text and/or a searchable PDF (Tesseract; feature-expansion phase, NEW)

fields.name: file
fields.description: The (scanned) PDF.

file.note: Only application/pdf is accepted (415 unsupported_media_type otherwise). Maximum file size and PDF page limits are plan/settings limits (runtime), see GET /v1/usage. The operation handles one file per run; send several files in this field and each is processed on its own, answered as one result per file. How many files one request may carry is set by the plan (files per request).

fields.name: languages
fields.description: 1-4 Tesseract language codes joined by "+" (GET /v1/formats lists the installed packs, which include every Tesseract language). A plan can limit the number of languages and whether non-core languages are allowed.

behavior.note: Bad syntax or not-installed pack -> 400 (details.allowed).

fields.name: deskew
fields.description: Straighten pages before OCR.

behavior.normalization: only "true" (case-insensitive) counts as true; any other value = false

fields.name: denoise
fields.description: Denoise pages before OCR.

behavior.normalization: only "true" (case-insensitive) counts as true; any other value = false

fields.name: clean
fields.description: Cleanup preprocessing.

behavior.normalization: only "true" (case-insensitive) counts as true; any other value = false

fields.name: output
fields.description: text = recognised text; pdf = searchable PDF; pdfa = searchable PDF/A; docx = Word document (LibreOffice); json = every word with confidence and box; tsv / hocr / alto = the engine layout formats as one file.

behavior.normalization: lower-cased; docx -> text then converted; pdfa -> pdf then converted

fields.name: mode
fields.description: auto (default) or table: tune recognition for tables (single block, spaces kept).

fields.name: tables
fields.description: Also detect the tables in the recognised text and return them as `tables`.

fields.name: force
fields.description: OCR every page even when it already has a text layer.

behavior.normalization: only "true" (case-insensitive) counts as true; any other value = false

fields.name: pages
fields.description: Pages: "all", "first", or a comma list of pages/ranges such as "1,3-5" (1-based). Default = all pages.

behavior.note: Lenient parser: out-of-range pages are dropped/clamped to the document; if nothing valid remains the result falls back to page 1 (it does NOT return an error).

fields.name: dpi
fields.description: Rasterization resolution for OCR.

fields.name: psm
fields.description: Tesseract page segmentation mode (1 and 3-13). 0 and 2 only detect the page orientation and read no text, so they are refused.

behavior.note: Outside [0,13], and 0 or 2, -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: output_bundle
fields.description: zip = return the result files of this request as ONE zip download (`bundle.url`) instead of one signed URL per file. It applies when the request produces two or more files (several input files, or an operation with several outputs); with a single result file the normal answer is returned. The files in `results` then carry `bundleEntry` (their place in the zip) instead of `url`. Not available together with `async: true`.

behavior.note: Any value other than zip -> 400 invalid_parameter. Combined with async: true -> 400 invalid_parameter. Results above 300 MB in total are not bundled: the answer lists the files as usual and carries `bundle_error`.

fields.name: validate_only
fields.description: true = check the request without running it. The answer is `{ validated: true, valid, errors[], files, estimate, limits }` instead of the endpoint's usual answer: `errors` lists every parameter or file the real call would reject, `estimate` is what it would count against your plan, and `limits` are the limits that apply to this endpoint for your key. Nothing is processed, no files are produced and no files are counted against the plan; the call itself counts as one request. It does not run the operation, so a problem that only shows while processing (a crop outside the image, an unreadable file) is not found.

behavior.normalization: only "true" enables it

fields.name: presetId
fields.description: Apply a saved preset (create one with POST /v1/presets). Every value stored in the preset is used unless this request sets that field itself. The preset must have been saved for this same endpoint; requires an individual customer API key.

fields.name: response
fields.description: How the result comes back. url (default) = the usual JSON answer with a signed URL per file. binary = the file itself as the HTTP body with Content-Type and Content-Disposition (a request with several result files returns one zip). base64 = the JSON answer with each result carrying `data` (base64) and `mimeType` instead of `url`, up to 20 MB in total. Answers without a result file are returned as JSON either way. Not available together with `async: true`.

behavior.normalization: lower-cased
behavior.note: Any other value -> 400 invalid_parameter. Combined with async: true (binary / base64) -> 400 invalid_parameter. Results above 300 MB (binary, several files) or 20 MB (base64) are not inlined: the JSON answer lists the files as usual and carries response_error / base64_error.

fields.name: filename
fields.description: The name for the result file (without extension; the extension follows the format). Used as the download name: Content-Disposition for response=binary, `downloadName` in the JSON answer otherwise. Path separators, control and bidirectional characters and Windows-reserved characters are removed; names are capped at 150 bytes. Several result files get -1, -2 ... added.

behavior.normalization: sanitised (never rejected for its characters); longer than 255 characters -> 400 invalid_parameter; together with filename_template -> 400 invalid_parameter

fields.name: filename_template
fields.description: A name built per result file from placeholders: {name} (the input file name without extension), {index} (1, 2, ...), {date} (YYYY-MM-DD), {time} (HH-MM-SS, UTC), {format} (the result extension) and {operation}. Example: "{name}-{index}-{date}". Sanitised like filename; result files that would get the same name are numbered -2, -3 ... Not together with filename.

behavior.note: An unknown placeholder or an unmatched brace -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: app
fields.description: The name of the app that makes this call, for example "My shop importer". It is shown in your History next to the result, so you can tell which app did what. The official apps fill it in themselves (Davix H2I plugin, Davix H2I n8n node, Davix H2I Studio, Davix H2I Customer Portal); when you leave it out, the official SDKs and plugins are recognised from their User-Agent. Up to 60 characters; control characters and angle brackets are removed. The header `X-Davix-App` does the same. It is only a label: it never changes what the call does.

behavior.normalization: plain text, one line, cut to 60 characters; blank = not set

fields.name: source_url
fields.description: Fetch the input from this public http(s) address instead of uploading a file in "file". Send either the file or source_url, not both. Only public addresses on port 80/443 are fetched (never loopback, private, link-local or cloud-metadata addresses), redirects are re-checked, and the download is size- and time-limited; the fetched file is then judged exactly like an upload (content sniffing, format and size limits).

behavior.note: Not an http(s) URL, credentials in the URL, or an address that is not public -> 400 url_blocked; a download that fails, is too slow or redirects too often -> 400 url_fetch_failed; larger than the limit -> 413 file_too_large; a plan without URL input -> 403 format_not_allowed.

fields.name: source_urls
fields.description: A list of public http(s) addresses to fetch as inputs, as a JSON array, for example ["https://example.com/a.pdf","https://example.com/b.pdf"]. They are added to any files you upload: uploaded files come first, then the URLs, in the order sent. Together they cannot exceed the files-per-request limit of your plan. Only public addresses on port 80/443 are fetched (never loopback, private, link-local or cloud-metadata addresses), redirects are re-checked, and the download is size- and time-limited; every fetched file is then judged exactly like an upload (content sniffing, format and size limits).

behavior.note: Not an http(s) URL, credentials in the URL, or an address that is not public -> 400 url_blocked; a download that fails, is too slow or redirects too often -> 400 url_fetch_failed; larger than the limit -> 413 file_too_large; a plan without URL input -> 403 format_not_allowed; a file and a URL for the same input -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: Idempotency-Key
fields.description: Optional idempotency key (8-128 characters). Reuse it for a retry of the SAME request; a different request with the same key -> 409 idempotency_key_conflict.

fields.name: async
fields.description: Opt-in asynchronous execution. With async=true and an individual customer API key the endpoint answers 202 {job_id, status_url} and the result becomes available from GET /v1/jobs/{id}. Omitted/false = the normal synchronous response. A request that carries several files in one field is not run as a job: it is processed immediately, answered with one result per file, and a `warnings` entry says that async was not applied.

behavior.normalization: only boolean true or the string "true" enables it
behavior.note: With any other key type the request is rejected with 400 async_requires_customer_key.

url.description: Searchable PDF, DOCX or PDF/A depending on output.

file_id.description: The file's id in your file history (customer keys only): pass it to GET /v1/files/{id} to fetch the file again, or DELETE /v1/files/{id} to delete it now.

format.description: The file format of `url` for tsv / hocr / alto output.

tables.description: Only with tables=true: the tables found in the recognised text (same shape as /v1/pdfs/tables).

endpoints.notes: Requires tesseract (and LibreOffice for output=docx/pdfa) on the server: runtime capabilities. The maximum pages per request is a server setting (default 20).

fields.name: imageQuality
fields.description: Quality for recompressed images.

behavior.note: Outside [1,100] or non-integer -> 400.

fields.name: imageColorSpace
fields.description: Convert recompressed images to this color space.

fields.name: repair
fields.description: Try to repair structural damage with qpdf.

behavior.normalization: only "true" (case-insensitive) counts as true; any other value = false

fields.name: profile
fields.description: engine=gs: screen (72 dpi), ebook (150), printer (300) or prepress (300). Sets the default downsampling resolution.

fields.name: downsample_dpi

fields.name: grayscale

fields.name: target_size_kb
fields.description: engine=gs: lower the image resolution step by step until the file is at most this size; the answer says whether it was reached (text and vector content are never degraded).

fields.name: linearize
fields.description: Make the result a "fast web view" PDF (linearized) after any engine.

fields.name: engine
fields.description: sharp = recompress images; qpdf = structural optimization; gs = Ghostscript (profiles, downsampling, grayscale, a target size). recompressImages requires engine=sharp.

fields.description: Document information: { title, author, subject, keywords (comma separated), creator }.

fields.name: pdfa
fields.description: Convert the result to PDF/A (1b, 2b or 3b) and validate it; the response says which level passed. Fails rather than claiming conformance that did not validate.

fields.name: validate_only
fields.description: true = check the request without running it. The answer is `{ validated: true, valid, errors[], files, estimate, limits }` instead of the endpoint's usual answer: `errors` lists every parameter or file the real call would reject, `estimate` is what it would count against your plan, and `limits` are the limits that apply to this endpoint for your key. Nothing is processed, no files are produced and no files are counted against the plan; the call itself counts as one request. It does not run the operation, so a problem that only shows while processing (a crop outside the image, an unreadable file) is not found.

behavior.normalization: only "true" enables it

fields.name: presetId
fields.description: Apply a saved preset (create one with POST /v1/presets). Every value stored in the preset is used unless this request sets that field itself. The preset must have been saved for this same endpoint; requires an individual customer API key.

fields.name: response
fields.description: How the result comes back. url (default) = the usual JSON answer with a signed URL per file. binary = the file itself as the HTTP body with Content-Type and Content-Disposition (a request with several result files returns one zip). base64 = the JSON answer with each result carrying `data` (base64) and `mimeType` instead of `url`, up to 20 MB in total. Answers without a result file are returned as JSON either way. Not available together with `async: true`.

behavior.normalization: lower-cased
behavior.note: Any other value -> 400 invalid_parameter. Combined with async: true (binary / base64) -> 400 invalid_parameter. Results above 300 MB (binary, several files) or 20 MB (base64) are not inlined: the JSON answer lists the files as usual and carries response_error / base64_error.

fields.name: filename
fields.description: The name for the result file (without extension; the extension follows the format). Used as the download name: Content-Disposition for response=binary, `downloadName` in the JSON answer otherwise. Path separators, control and bidirectional characters and Windows-reserved characters are removed; names are capped at 150 bytes. Several result files get -1, -2 ... added.

behavior.normalization: sanitised (never rejected for its characters); longer than 255 characters -> 400 invalid_parameter; together with filename_template -> 400 invalid_parameter

fields.name: filename_template
fields.description: A name built per result file from placeholders: {name} (the input file name without extension), {index} (1, 2, ...), {date} (YYYY-MM-DD), {time} (HH-MM-SS, UTC), {format} (the result extension) and {operation}. Example: "{name}-{index}-{date}". Sanitised like filename; result files that would get the same name are numbered -2, -3 ... Not together with filename.

behavior.note: An unknown placeholder or an unmatched brace -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: app
fields.description: The name of the app that makes this call, for example "My shop importer". It is shown in your History next to the result, so you can tell which app did what. The official apps fill it in themselves (Davix H2I plugin, Davix H2I n8n node, Davix H2I Studio, Davix H2I Customer Portal); when you leave it out, the official SDKs and plugins are recognised from their User-Agent. Up to 60 characters; control characters and angle brackets are removed. The header `X-Davix-App` does the same. It is only a label: it never changes what the call does.

behavior.normalization: plain text, one line, cut to 60 characters; blank = not set

fields.name: Idempotency-Key
fields.description: Optional idempotency key (8-128 characters). Reuse it for a retry of the SAME request; a different request with the same key -> 409 idempotency_key_conflict.

fields.name: async
fields.description: Opt-in asynchronous execution. With async=true and an individual customer API key the endpoint answers 202 {job_id, status_url} and the result becomes available from GET /v1/jobs/{id}. Omitted/false = the normal synchronous response. A request that carries several files in one field is not run as a job: it is processed immediately, answered with one result per file, and a `warnings` entry says that async was not applied.

behavior.normalization: only boolean true or the string "true" enables it
behavior.note: With any other key type the request is rejected with 400 async_requires_customer_key.

response.description: One document: { url, file_id, ... }. With records: { results: [{ url, format, sizeBytes, record, ... }] }, one result per record.

url.description: The result file (one document). With records the answer is `results` instead.

file_id.description: The file's id in your file history (customer keys only): pass it to GET /v1/files/{id} to fetch the file again, or DELETE /v1/files/{id} to delete it now.

bookmarks.description: Number of bookmarks written (only when outline was requested).

pdfa.description: The PDF/A level that validated (only when pdfa was requested).

file_id.description: The file's id in your file history (customer keys only).

endpoints.notes: Network access from the rendered page is SSRF-protected (private/internal addresses are blocked). With `records` every document counts as one unit unless the plan says otherwise (records per unit); the answer is { results: [{ url, format, sizeBytes, record, ... }] }.

endpoints.name: The authenticated customer's own subscription status, plan detail, and current usage (Customer Portal, NEW).
endpoints.notes: ACCOUNT-SPECIFIC runtime data (plan, entitlements, limits, usage). Not part of the static contract.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: Only return templates of this kind.

behavior.note: An unknown kind returns an empty list.

response.description: Your templates (without their html/css) and the plan limit.

limit.description: The most templates the plan allows (empty = no plan limit).

endpoints.name: Create a template
endpoints.description: Save an HTML document with {{variables}} to render later with templateId (html-to-pdf, html-to-image). A template holds content only; the settings of a render stay in presets or in the request.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Template name (1-100 characters after trimming); unique per account.

behavior.normalization: trimmed
behavior.note: Duplicate name -> 409 duplicate_template_name. The number of templates is limited by the plan.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: html (the only kind created here). DOCX / ODT templates for mail-merge are created with POST /v1/templates/upload.

behavior.note: Another kind -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: description
fields.description: A short note about the template (up to 300 characters).

fields.name: html
fields.description: The document, with {{name}} / {{a.b}} placeholders. A placeholder that is the whole value of src, href or a CSS url() takes a web address or an image data: URI; everywhere else its value is HTML-escaped. No expression language: a value can never become markup or script.

dynamicLimit.description: The maximum length is plan-specific (the HTML size limit and the largest template).

fields.name: css
fields.description: CSS for the document; {{variables}} in it are filled too (their values may not contain braces, semicolons, quotes, angle brackets, backslashes or comments).

fields.name: variables
fields.description: Details of the variables the html and css use. The variables themselves are found automatically from {{name}} placeholders; list one here only to give it a default, mark it required or describe it. A name the text does not use is refused.

properties.name: name
properties.description: A variable the text uses, e.g. customer_name or customer.name.

properties.name: default
properties.description: Used when a request leaves this variable empty.

properties.name: required
properties.description: When true, a request that leaves it empty (and no default) is refused.

properties.name: description
properties.description: A note for whoever uses the template.

response.description: The created template, with the variables found in it.

endpoints.notes: Requires an individual customer API key (templates are account-scoped). The plan sets how many templates, the largest template and the endpoints they may be used on. A {{...}} that is not a valid variable name is listed in `warnings`.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Template id.

response.description: Deleted. No response body.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Template id.

response.description: The template with its html, css and variables.

fields.name: id

fields.name: name
fields.description: New name (1-100 characters).

fields.name: description
fields.description: New note (up to 300 characters).

fields.name: html

fields.name: css
fields.description: The new CSS.

fields.name: variables
fields.description: Details of the variables the html and css use. The variables themselves are found automatically from {{name}} placeholders; list one here only to give it a default, mark it required or describe it. A name the text does not use is refused.

properties.name: name
properties.description: A variable the text uses, e.g. customer_name or customer.name.

properties.name: default
properties.description: Used when a request leaves this variable empty.

properties.name: required
properties.description: When true, a request that leaves it empty (and no default) is refused.

properties.name: description
properties.description: A note for whoever uses the template.

response.description: The updated template.

endpoints.notes: Requires an individual customer API key.

endpoints.name: Replace the file of a DOCX / ODT template
endpoints.description: Upload a new DOCX or ODT file for an existing file template. Details already given for a variable survive as long as the new file still uses its name.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Template id.

fields.name: file
fields.description: The new DOCX or ODT template.

file.note: At most 4 MB, and never more than your plan allows for a template.

fields.name: variables
fields.description: Details of the variables (default, required, description) as a JSON array; omitted = keep the details already saved.

response.description: The updated template.

endpoints.notes: Requires an individual customer API key.

endpoints.name: Create a DOCX / ODT template
endpoints.description: Save a Word (DOCX) or OpenDocument (ODT) file with {{variables}} to fill with POST /v1/documents/mail-merge and templateId. The variables are found in the text of the document (headers, footers and footnotes included).

fields.name: name
fields.description: Template name (1-100 characters after trimming); unique per account.

behavior.normalization: trimmed
behavior.note: Duplicate name -> 409 duplicate_template_name.

fields.name: description
fields.description: A short note about the template (up to 300 characters).

fields.name: file
fields.description: The DOCX or ODT template. Macro-enabled and oversized packages are refused (400).

file.note: At most 4 MB, and never more than your plan allows for a template (largest template).

fields.name: variables
fields.description: Details of the variables the document uses (default, required, description), as a JSON array of { name, default, required, description }. The variables themselves are found automatically.

response.description: The created template, with the variables found in the document.

endpoints.notes: Requires an individual customer API key. The plan sets how many templates you can keep and the largest template.

endpoints.name: The authenticated customer's own usage: current-period snapshot, per-category totals, recent period history, and (if they have more than one key) a per-key breakdown (Customer Portal, NEW).

fields.name: months
fields.description: How many past billing periods to include.

behavior.note: Clamped to [1,24]; non-numeric -> 6.

history.description: Recent plan periods (newest first), summed over all of the customer keys: period, used_files, reserved_files, used_bytes, total_calls, total_files_processed, per-category calls/files, bytes_in, bytes_out, errors, last_request_at.

by_key.description: Attribution of the shared quota: one entry per API key of the customer (api_key_id, label, key_prefix or key_last4, period, used_files in the plan unit, by_category, quota_limit, expires_at, expired) plus one Studio entry (studio: true) for the web sign-in keys. A deleted key is not listed; what it used still counts in current and history.

metered.description: Plan meters: meter_key, label, unit, used, limit, window_type, window_seconds, match_type, match_value, resets_at.

endpoints.notes: ACCOUNT-SPECIFIC runtime data (plan usage, remaining quota). Not part of the static contract.

endpoints.name: Usage activity behind the usage page: per day, per operation, why requests failed, per key, AI cost and jobs, plus what the plan includes

fields.name: range
fields.description: The time window: the current plan period so far (default), the last 7 days, the last 30 days, or the current calendar month (UTC). The previous window of the same length is reported for comparison.

behavior.note: Any other value -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: key_id
fields.description: Only this API key (an id from the by-key list), or "studio" for the web sign-in keys. Omitted = all of your keys, deleted ones included in the totals.

behavior.note: A key that is not yours -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: key
fields.description: Deprecated name of key_id. Production rejects a query parameter called key (api_key_location_not_allowed), so use key_id.

behavior.note: In production any query parameter named key -> 400 api_key_location_not_allowed. Use key_id.

window.description: range, since, until (the window that was read).

days.description: One entry per UTC day of the window: date, files, requests, errors, by_category. Also ai_tokens and ai_cost_usd: what AI calls used that day.

totals.description: files, requests, errors, bytes_in, bytes_out for the window.

previous.description: files, requests, errors for the previous window of the same length.

operations.description: Per operation: key (category:operation), label, category, category_label, files, requests, errors, bytes_in, bytes_out, last_used.

errors.description: Why requests failed: code, title, hint, count, last_at.

keys.description: Per API key: api_key_id, label, files, requests, errors, last_used.

ai.description: AI calls, tokens and estimated cost (USD) in the window; null when the plan has no AI or nothing was used.

plan.description: name, slug, is_free, monthly_limit_files (null = unlimited), categories (only those the plan includes: key, label, monthly_limit_files), jobs (allowed, max_active, queue_wait_seconds, active_now), rate_limits, allowance (the plan's allowance: total, shared pool, and how each kind of work draws from it, AI in tokens or dollars included), detail_retention_days.

jobs.description: Jobs of the last 30 days by status; null when the plan does not allow jobs.

notifications.description: The notification preferences (same entries as GET /v1/notifications/preferences).

endpoints.notes: ACCOUNT-SPECIFIC runtime data. The `plan` block lists only the categories the plan includes; a limit of null means unlimited, and what was used is still reported. Request details are kept for plan.detail_retention_days.

endpoints.name: Request log of your keys (time, status, request id, key, operation, size, and the reason for a failure), optionally of one operation

fields.name: operation
fields.description: Only this operation as listed by /v1/usage/breakdown: "category:operation", for example "image:resize". Omitted = every request of the window.

behavior.note: An unknown category -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: key_id
fields.description: Only this API key (an id), or "studio". Omitted = all of your keys.

behavior.note: A key that is not yours -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: key
fields.description: Deprecated name of key_id. Production rejects a query parameter called key (api_key_location_not_allowed), so use key_id.

behavior.note: In production any query parameter named key -> 400 api_key_location_not_allowed. Use key_id.

fields.name: limit
fields.description: How many requests to return, newest first.

behavior.note: Clamped to [1,200]; non-numeric -> 20.

fields.name: range
fields.description: The time window of the log: the current plan period so far (default), the last 7 days, the last 30 days, or the current calendar month (UTC).

behavior.note: Any other value -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: before
fields.description: Paging: the next_before of the previous page. Returns the requests older than that one.

behavior.note: Not a positive whole number -> 400 invalid_parameter.

fields.name: page
fields.description: Page number (1 = the newest requests). Ignored when `before` is given.

behavior.note: Not a whole number from 1 -> 400 invalid_parameter.

total.description: Every request of the window (and operation), not only this page.

next_before.description: Pass as before to get the next page; null on the last page.

calls.description: Newest first: id, at, status, request_id, key, operation (key, label, category, category_label), files, bytes_in, bytes_out, app, ip, user_agent and, for a failure, error (code, title, hint, message).

endpoints.notes: ACCOUNT-SPECIFIC runtime data, kept for the plan.detail_retention_days reported by /v1/usage/breakdown.

capabilities.description: What the API contract guarantees. Independent of the deployment (see GET /v1/capabilities for installed tools/encoders/languages) and of the account (see GET /v1/usage and GET /v1/subscription for plan limits and remaining quota).
